title: Pilot network posture proof on portfolio-devbox
description: Pilot the new posture against portfolio-devbox with an operator-safe plan. This Bead should not start by changing live firewall state; first collect current cloud firewall, host firewall/listener, public probe, Tailnet probe, and app exposure evidence, then decide whether any live migration is needed. Model route and authority: Codex gpt-5.5 owns orchestration, system design, implementation, review, commit acceptance, and final say. Claude Opus is only for UX/docs visual review if a docs surface needs design judgment. Grok/Composer 2.5 may run bounded probes only when the validation commands and stronger-model review are explicit. Stop condition: if applying firewall changes could lock out access, require an explicit staged plan and recovery path before mutation.
acceptance_criteria: Acceptance: evidence artifact proves current portfolio-devbox posture or lists exact drift; if mutation is needed, dry-run, backup/recovery path, and post-change verification are recorded before action. Validation: public TCP probes are from an external/operator vantage point, DO firewall inspection is redacted, Tailnet SSH still works, and no app ports become public.
notes: No-ragrets contract. Outcome: portfolio-devbox proves the lifecycle on a real instance before future boxes depend on it. Evidence: redacted cloud firewall state, host listener/firewall state, external public probes, Tailnet probes, app exposure proof, dry-run and recovery plan before any mutation. Failure avoided: code ships without discovering live-box sequencing or lockout risks.
close_reason: Posture proof collected: box is functionally locked down (SSH key-auth denied, Tailnet works), one drift item (cloud_firewall_missing). Evidence and migration plan in WG-portfolio-devbox-posture-pilot_RESULT.md

title: DWS worker_done over SBP: authenticated host-side receipt intake
description:
Outcome: an Amp Orb finishes a sealed DWS handoff with one public SBP command; SBP transports a compact completion report to the host; private DWS builds and validates its own internal delivery receipt. Orb never hand-authors dws-delivery-receipt/v1 and never writes dispatcher-local file://.

Verified defect: do-work-son-evidence.py sends file:///srv/skillbox/state/amp/delivery-receipts/<admission>.json into isolated Orbs; dispatcher receives zero files. Current sbpd is GET-only; sbp_client supports cass and skill.

Implement public Skillbox transport only:
- Add sbp dws complete to scripts/sbp and the orb-kit client. Input: sealed handoff plus small worker result. Produce versioned dws-worker-result/v1 envelope, not private receipt.
- Add authenticated POST intake behind explicit default-OFF worker-write flag and configured private inbox.
- Bind Amp JWT project_id to selected_project_id; admission path/body; handoff_digest; lease_id; positive fencing_token; repo_id; bead_id; base_sha.
- Atomic bounded write; reject symlink/non-regular targets. Exact replay idempotent; conflicting digest 409.
- Response accepted_pending_reconciliation only. No Bead close, lease release, arbitrary path, command delegation, private schema validation, service restart, or deployment.

Write scope: scripts/sbpd.py; scripts/lib/sbp_client.py; scripts/sbp; tests/test_sbpd.py; tests/test_sbp_client.py; tests/test_cli_wrappers.py; docs/orb-tailnet-bootstrap.md; new narrowly named tests/helpers. Do not touch dirty policy_eval.py, gen_output_schemas.py, test_output_schema_docs.py.

Acceptance:
1. Fresh orb kit contains sbp dws complete and a test reaches configured host inbox through SBP_REMOTE.
2. Tests refuse unauthenticated/wrong-project/wrong-admission/invalid fence/oversize/symlink/conflicting replay; exact replay idempotent.
3. POST absent unless explicit flag plus inbox.
4. Envelope contains sufficient immutable handoff/result data for private DWS conversion without trusting filename.
5. Run python3 -m unittest -v tests.test_sbpd tests.test_sbp_client tests.test_cli_wrappers; python3 -m ruff check touched Python/tests; bash -n scripts/sbp; git diff --check.
6. Commit and push only after focused tests pass; report exact SHA and evidence.

title: Lube: fold sbp recalibrate into skill-invoke failure path to cut 3-step visibility ceremony
description:
CASS evidence: 210 'missing_for_cwd' events, 133 'sbp recalibrate', 67 'sbp skill activate' across 500 recent sessions. The pattern is always the same: agent invokes a skill → skill not visible → agent runs sbp recalibrate → discovers missing_for_cwd → runs sbp skill activate → retries. This 3-step chain burns 2-5 tool calls per occurrence.

No-ragrets success contract:
- Outcome: when a skill invocation fails because the skill is not visible, the failure message includes the exact 'sbp skill activate <skill> --cwd $PWD' command to run, or the sbp recalibrate step auto-runs and reports what to activate
- Evidence: future sessions contain at most 1 sbp command per skill visibility miss instead of 3
- Failure avoided: agents abandoning skill-based work and falling back to ad-hoc improvisation because the recovery ceremony is too long

Lube unblocker: option A (smallest): make the 'skill not loaded' system-reminder include the activate command. Option B (durable): add a --auto-fix flag to sbp recalibrate that auto-activates missing_for_cwd skills with dry-run output. Either way, the 3-step chain becomes 1 step.
notes: Included in no-ragrets high-use weak-surface slate skillbox-high-use-weak-surfaces-no-ragrets-fxm8. User agreed this is a future pass candidate: collapse missing skill visibility recovery from sbp recalibrate + activate ceremony into one exact command or auto-fix path.
close_reason: Closed by mion.20: sbp recalibrate --auto-fix --yes now has E2E coverage proving missing skill recovery collapses to one outer sbp command with same-command activation packet and effective visibility afterward.

title: Lube: sbp cass status fast-path — health+probe first, skip 2-minute DB stats timeout
description:
CASS evidence: 736 hits for 'sbp cass status error', 97 for 'cass health unhealthy stale', 283 for 'cass index stale run rebuild'. Every cass-using session starts with sbp cass status, which ran cass status --json (full 2GB DB stats pass, 45s timeout default) before falling back to the cheap cass health (2ms) + search probe. Agents paid 30-120s of blocked time every session.

No-ragrets success contract:
- Outcome: sbp cass status returns in <5s by running cass health + search probe first (the fast path). The expensive cass status --json is only run when --full is explicitly requested.
- Evidence: before-fix sbp cass status timed out at 124; after-fix returns ok in 4.5s with 232K search matches confirmed.
- Failure avoided: every cass-using agent session losing 2+ minutes to a timeout wall before getting the same answer the cheap probe provides.
- Acceptance: (1) sbp cass status (no flags) returns health+probe in <5s, (2) sbp cass status --full runs the expensive path for diagnostics, (3) all 10 existing tests pass with updated coverage for fast/full paths.
close_reason: Fix applied: sbp_cass.py status() now runs cheap health+probe by default (4.5s), with --full flag for expensive DB stats. 10/10 tests pass.

title: box.py teardown leaks the DigitalOcean volume (no detach/delete on down)
description: cmd_down/_destroy_box_droplet (scripts/box.py ~2920-3003) deletes the droplet but never detaches or deletes the DO volume that _ensure_box_storage (~1889) created and attached during provision. Result: (1) every teardown orphans a paid DO volume; (2) re-provisioning the same box_id can fail with 'already attached ... Detach it before reusing' (~1915) because do_find_volume_by_name finds the same-named volume still bound to the deleted droplet. The dry-run preview (_emit_box_down_dry_run ~2881) only mentions the droplet, so the gap is invisible on review. Fix: after droplet deletion, if box.volume_id is set, best-effort detach then 'doctl compute volume delete <id> --force'; surface a 'volume' step in BOTH the dry-run and real payloads; guard against deleting a volume still attached elsewhere. Found during 2026-05-23 fresh-eyes audit; intentionally NOT auto-fixed because it is a destructive change that cannot be tested against live doctl without infra.
close_reason: Fixed and validated

title: Lube: make doctor should emit fix commands for common failures instead of just diagnostics
description:
CASS evidence: 171 agent-initiated 'make doctor' invocations across 500 recent sessions, 144 of which contained error/fail content. Agents run doctor, see a wall of diagnostics, then must interpret the error and guess the fix command. This is the second-highest friction category after sbp ceremony.

No-ragrets success contract:
- Outcome: when make doctor detects a fixable drift (stale render, missing dependency, unsynced beads, etc.), it emits a 'suggested fix' line with the exact shell command to run
- Evidence: agent sessions that encounter doctor failures resolve in 1 tool call (copy-paste the fix) instead of 3-5 (read output, research cause, try fix, rerun doctor)
- Failure avoided: agents getting stuck in doctor-interpret-fix-rerun loops, or skipping doctor entirely because the output is too noisy to act on

Lube unblocker: extend scripts/04-reconcile.py or the Makefile doctor target to emit a 'fix:' JSON field or plaintext line for each actionable finding. Start with the top 3 most common failures: stale render (fix: make render), missing .beads/ init (fix: sbp beads init --cwd .), and unsynced beads (fix: br sync --flush-only).

title: Lube: cass freshness probe is blind to the recency ceiling — 'fresh' while newest indexed session is 5 weeks old
description:
Found 2026-08-02 lube mining pass. sbp cass status reported probe fresh (last-probe-ok 2026-08-02T09:02:08Z, matches=483942) while the index's newest date bucket was 2026-06-28 and searches for known-recent identifiers (skillbox-5gth, seamless-remote-image-paste — both active in the last week) returned total_matches=0. The probe only asserts 'a wildcard search returned matches', never 'recent sessions are searchable'. Consequence: agents are instructed to 'proceed directly to mining — the cron keeps the index fresh every 30 minutes' and then mine a corpus with a 5-week recency hole without any signal. staleness_guard (commit 80b4d43 in skillbox-config) catches an OLD probe, not a fresh probe over stale CONTENT. Related but distinct: skillbox-config-3pd4 (index backlog/cap — the cause), skillbox-ztaa (dead probe).

No-ragrets success contract:
- Outcome: sbp cass status and last-probe-ok carry a newest_indexed_session date (e.g. via a date-bucketed probe or max(timestamp) query), and status degrades with an explicit reason when that date is older than 72h.
- Evidence: 'sbp cass status --json' shows newest_indexed_session; with today's stale index it reports degraded/content-stale instead of fresh; after backlog drains it reports ok and a search for a <48h-old session identifier returns hits.
- Failure avoided: future mining/evidence passes silently reach conclusions from a month-old corpus and file beads/reports labeled 'recent' that aren't.

title: Lube: sbp cass search text output shows results instead of empty metadata
description:
CASS evidence: 520 hits for cass search empty/fallback patterns, 133 for agents falling back to grep after getting empty-looking results. The sbp cass search text renderer (non-JSON mode) only printed the base payload header (index_host, data_dir, etc.) and omitted the actual search hits entirely. Agents who didn't know to pass --json saw zero useful output and concluded the search was broken.

No-ragrets success contract:
- Outcome: sbp cass search (text mode) prints a compact hit summary with query, hit count, total matches, and per-hit source file + title + snippet. --json mode is unchanged.
- Evidence: direct observation — sbp cass search 'query' printed only 5 metadata lines with no results. After fix: prints hits with source, title, snippet.
- Failure avoided: agents concluding cass search is broken because the text output shows nothing, falling back to raw grep across transcript files.
- Acceptance: (1) text output includes hit count and per-hit summary, (2) --json output unchanged, (3) 12/12 tests pass.
close_reason: Fix applied: _emit_search_text() in sbp_cass.py renders query, hit count/total, per-hit source + title + snippet. 12/12 tests pass.

title: Lube: sbp cass mine-friction compound — automate the multi-search friction-pattern extraction this session does manually
description:
CASS evidence: this session (1d7110c9) itself demonstrates the friction: mining cass for repeated agent pain requires 10+ individual sbp cass search calls, manual JSON parsing, file reading to understand hit content (which isn't returned inline), and Counter-based frequency analysis. The evidence miner partially covers this but produces skill-level opportunity cards, not session-friction-frequency analysis.

The pattern that agents need is: "show me the top N repeated friction patterns across recent sessions, ranked by frequency × impact." This session ran ~15 cass search calls to produce what could be one compound command.

No-ragrets success contract:
- Outcome: a single sbp cass mine-friction (or lube_evidence_miner --mode friction-frequency) command emits ranked friction patterns with counts, affected sessions, and lube-target classification.
- Evidence: the next agent that needs to identify friction targets gets ranked results in 1 command instead of 15.
- Failure avoided: agents spending 10+ tool calls and 50KB+ of context on the mining ceremony itself, or giving up on cass mining because the ergonomics are too poor.

Lube unblocker: extend lube_evidence_miner.py (or create sbp cass mine-friction) with a --mode frequency that: (1) searches for known friction signal terms in batch, (2) counts sessions per pattern, (3) ranks by frequency × token-waste, (4) emits the lube output shape. Input: the same cass search backend. Output: ranked friction patterns ready for bead creation.
close_reason: Implemented lube_evidence_miner.py --mode frequency in canonical skills repo (/srv/skillbox/repos/skills, commit 38de8e3) and synced the deployed copy at ~/.claude/skills/lube/. Batch-searches 10 curated friction patterns via sbp cass search --json, dedupes per (source_path,line), ranks by unique-session-count x approx token waste, emits ranked JSON with pattern/lube_target/score/session_ids/sample_snippet. Live run against real cass index (exit 0): top-5 = context-compression (27 sessions), permission-prompt-friction (30), tui-blocked (29), retry-loop (20), timeout (14). Tests: 6 passed (unit + mocked-backend e2e + --help). SKILL.md documents the mode as the replacement for manual multi-search mining. Default --mode evidence behavior regression-checked unchanged.

comments.author: skillbox
comments.text:
2026-08-01 hardening sweep — root cause identified and partially fixed; full inventory below.

KEY INSIGHT (why this survived a week of local fixing): scripts/self-test.sh runs the suite against a 'git archive' extract with a PINNED toolchain (.skillbox-state/self-test/toolchain/py/3.1{1,2,3}), under TMPDIR=/srv/skillbox/tmp. That is a materially different world from a working checkout — no .git, no untracked files (.dcg.toml, skill-repos.lock.json), no synced skill source repos, and a working directory that is itself under the /srv/skillbox prefix that the estate-leak firewall guards. A suite that is green locally can and does fail all three lanes under the gate. Commit 8ea82fd was exactly that: locally green, gate red.

FIXED so far (commit 3e37445, verified in BOTH a working checkout and a real archive extract with the pinned 3.13 toolchain):
- test_oss_hygiene called 'git ls-files' with check=True -> ERROR in an archive (not a git repo). Now falls back to walking the tree; in an archive every present file IS a tracked file, so the invariant is unchanged.
- test_context_drift_goldens pinned two state-dependent tokens: the resolved skill set, and the sync verb (exists vs symlink-context). Both normalized the same way this module already normalizes host pressure and the fixture root; _check now normalizes BOTH sides so the JSON golden gets the same treatment as the markdown ones.
- Added test_dry_run_actions_use_only_known_sync_verbs so normalizing the verb does not cost the ability to catch a renamed verb. Verified that guard fails when handed an unknown verb.

REMAINING: 23 failures/errors under gate conditions (2870 tests, 10 failures + 13 errors). Full list: /srv/skillbox/state/hardening-20260801/gate-failure-inventory.txt; full log: gate-repro-3.13.log. Clusters:
- test_dcg_reconcile (6 errors) — FileNotFoundError on <tmp>/home/.claude/settings.json; likely depends on the dcg binary or fixture state absent from an archive (dcg is 'sync mode manual' and skipped by manage.py sync)
- module-level ImportErrors: test_audit_rows, test_sbpd, test_safety_gate_matrix, test_overlay_regression, test_mode_pack_overlays, test_fleet_e2e
- fleet/skill-default, alias-root folding, rollback, markdown link resolution, exit-code separation

METHOD THAT WORKS (much faster than the 65-min gate): extract and run directly —
  W=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/skbx.XXXXXX"); git archive HEAD | tar -x -C "$W"; cd "$W"
  <repo>/.skillbox-state/self-test/toolchain/py/3.13/bin/python -m unittest <module>
That reproduces a gate lane in seconds-to-minutes instead of ~21. 'scripts/self-test.sh --lane test-3.13' is the sanctioned single-lane path (~21 min).

Acceptance unchanged: all three python lanes green in a receipt whose canonical flag is true, with no assertion weakened to get there.

title: Lube: tighten cass and sbp skill contracts per evidence miner unclear-contract findings
description:
CASS evidence: lube evidence miner scored both cass (111 score, 15/16 runs) and sbp (119 score, 28/28 runs) as 'unclear skill contract' — the top friction card for both skills. Agents misapply skills, attempt non-goals, or use wrong subcommands because the SKILL.md contracts don't specify branch rules and non-goals sharply enough.

No-ragrets success contract:
- Outcome: cass SKILL.md and sbp SKILL.md each gain explicit non-goals, default-branch rules, and a 'do NOT' section that prevents the top 3 misapplication patterns observed in CASS evidence
- Evidence: evidence miner re-score for both skills drops from 'unclear skill contract' to a lower-priority card
- Failure avoided: agents wasting 3-5 tool calls per session discovering what a skill does not do, or falling back to improvisation because the contract is ambiguous

Lube unblocker: use /skill-issue to audit and tighten both SKILL.md files. For cass: clarify that cass is a search/query tool, not a direct file reader; specify auto-rebuild behavior. For sbp: clarify the recalibrate vs activate vs sync distinction; add non-goals for global skill installation and mass pruning.

title: Publish checksummed release tarballs so curl fallback verifies by default
description: From installer-workmanship pass (m19o.6): the git-less curl fallback in install.sh downloads a GitHub auto-generated archive with no published SHA256, forcing users into --sha256 (they cannot know the digest) or --allow-unverified. Release engineering should publish skillbox-<tag>.tar.gz + SHA256SUMS as release assets and install.sh should fetch and verify them by default. Acceptance: curl path verifies checksum without user-provided digest; test covers the verified download path.
close_reason: Release-engineering path landed: scripts/make-release-tarball.sh builds skillbox-<tag>.tar.gz + SHA256SUMS deterministically (git archive|gzip -n); .github/workflows/release.yml publishes them as release assets on tag push. install.sh download_source_tarball() now prefers download_release_assets() which fetches the published tarball + SHA256SUMS for a tagged ref and verifies the checksum BY DEFAULT (RELEASE_ASSET_VERIFIED flag satisfies verify_checksum with no --sha256), falling back to the GitHub auto-generated archive only when no release asset exists. Tests in tests/test_install_release.py cover verified download, tampered-tarball rejection, and missing-asset fallback (curl mocked). bash -n clean; 24/24 install tests pass. HUMAN FOLLOW-UP: cut the first tag (e.g. v0.1.0) so the workflow publishes a real signed release to exercise the path end-to-end against live GitHub.

title: Lube: route sbp mcp sync to manage.py mcp sync renderer

The manage.py mcp sync renderer exists and writes both files from a single declaration, but sbp mcp only exposed the read-only audit. - Acceptance: (1) sbp mcp sync --help shows the renderer, (2) sbp mcp sync --dry-run previews the diff, (3) sbp mcp (no subcommand) still runs the audit, (4) help text updated.

title: Fuzzy suggestions + bare-word resolution for explain/graph/search
description:
OBJECTIVE: When explain/graph/search receive an unknown or ambiguous target, return ranked suggestions and resolve unambiguous bare words automatically — turning UNKNOWN_NODE dead-ends into one-turn recoveries.

BACKGROUND: brain.explain takes typed node ids (e.g. command:brain.next, service:pulse). The first dogfood run (recorded in bead skillbox-smart-1-dogfood-friction-2c14, 2026-06-11) hit UNKNOWN_NODE on bare words like `pulse` with no recovery hint. Agents then burn a turn on search or guess the prefix grammar. The graph already holds every node id + kind; difflib is stdlib.

REASONING: the brain's promise is read-first self-description; an error that says only "unknown" on a near-miss contradicts the product. Suggestion quality here compounds across every agent session forever.

IMPLEMENTATION CONSIDERATIONS: (1) Resolution order for a bare word W: exact id match across kinds -> if exactly one, resolve and note resolved_from; if multiple, return AMBIGUOUS_NODE with the candidate list (kind-qualified) — do NOT guess. (2) On no match: difflib.get_close_matches over the full node-id corpus + command ids + skill names, cutoff tuned so garbage returns empty; payload gains suggestions:[{id, kind, score}] capped at 5; error code stays UNKNOWN_NODE (consumers depend on it) with the additions. (3) Same treatment for graph --algorithm unknown values (suggest from the algorithm registry) and search empty-result responses (suggest broader terms from index keys — cheap version: top related ids by substring). (4) Text renderer prints suggestions as copy-pasteable explain commands.

FILES: runtime_manager/agent_decisions.py (explain_payload), agent_graph_engine.py, agent_search.py, text_renderers.py, tests/test_agent_ops_decisions.py + search tests, goldens (one regen).

RISKS: suggestion noise on tiny corpora (cutoff + cap handle it); ambiguity resolution changing existing behavior for currently-working bare words (audit: if bare words currently NEVER resolve, auto-resolve is purely additive — verify before enabling).

ACCEPTANCE: (1) explain pulse resolves (single match) with resolved_from noted; (2) explain pluse returns UNKNOWN_NODE + suggestions including service:pulse; (3) ambiguous bare word lists candidates without resolving; (4) graph --algorithm critcal-path suggests critical-path; (5) goldens updated once; (6) friction items from 2c14 reproduced as tests and green.

TESTING: table-driven resolution tests (exact/unique/ambiguous/garbage); golden updates; renderer snapshot.

OBSERVABILITY: payloads carry resolved_from/suggestions — no extra logging needed.

MAINTAINER NOTES: Suggestions are capped and ranked; resist fuzzy AUTO-resolution (typo guessing) — suggest, never silently substitute a near-miss. resolved_from exists so transcripts stay auditable.
notes: Included in no-ragrets high-use weak-surface slate skillbox-high-use-weak-surfaces-no-ragrets-fxm8. User agreed this is a future pass candidate: UNKNOWN_NODE and bare-word misses should recover intent with suggestions instead of costing retry turns.
close_reason: Implemented fuzzy suggestions and bare-word resolution for explain/graph/search

title: snap ergonomics: flag-position tolerance + structured usage payload
description:
OBJECTIVE: Align `snap` argument ergonomics with its sibling brain commands — top-level --format, discoverable subcommand help, and consistent read/write defaults — removing the surface inconsistency the first dogfood run tripped on.

BACKGROUND: capabilities/next/graph/explain/search all accept --format json directly; snap requires a subcommand first (snap create/diff/replay) and the dogfood session (bead 2c14) noted the asymmetry costs a turn each time (error, retry with subcommand). snap is also the only brain command with a write mode (create --write), making its help disproportionately important.

REASONING: surface consistency is agent ergonomics — agents generalize patterns across sibling commands; every exception is a future wasted turn multiplied by every future session.

IMPLEMENTATION CONSIDERATIONS: (1) Bare `manage.py snap` (no subcommand) returns a structured usage payload (json: {subcommands, examples, read_only_default:true}) instead of an argparse error — exit 0 in json mode since it answered the implicit question. (2) Accept --format both before and after the subcommand (argparse parents or post-parse normalization in _normalize_agent_argv, which already exists for flag aliases — extend it). (3) Audit the read/write contract copy: create prints redacted snapshot by default, writes ONLY with --write — ensure help text + registry examples + README agree verbatim. (4) Keep MCP mirror (skillbox_snap) contract unchanged; add the usage payload there too for argument-free calls. (5) Registry examples updated; goldens regenerated once.

FILES: runtime_manager/cli.py (snap parser + normalize), command_registry.py examples, mcp_server.py, tests/test_agent_ops_snapshots.py + cli tests, goldens.

RISKS: argparse subparser quirks with interleaved flags (the normalize-layer approach sidesteps parser surgery); exit-code semantics for bare snap (json consumers: 0 with usage payload; text mode: keep nonzero usage error for script-safety — document the asymmetry).

ACCEPTANCE: (1) snap --format json replay <fixture> works flag-first; (2) bare snap in json mode returns the usage payload exit 0; (3) text mode keeps a helpful usage error; (4) all snap examples in registry/README copy-paste clean; (5) goldens stable after one regen.

TESTING: argv permutation tests through main(); MCP mirror test; help/usage snapshot tests.

OBSERVABILITY: n/a.

MAINTAINER NOTES: The normalize layer is the designated home for ergonomic aliasing — prefer extending it over per-command parser hacks, so consistency rules accrete in one place.
notes: Included in no-ragrets high-use weak-surface slate skillbox-high-use-weak-surfaces-no-ragrets-fxm8. User agreed this is a future pass candidate: snap should match sibling brain command ergonomics for flag placement and structured usage.
close_reason: Completed snap usage payload, flag-first replay, MCP no-action parity, and tests

title: Brain latency budget + perf proof harness + elapsed_ms meta
description:
OBJECTIVE: Establish and enforce a latency budget for the brain's read surfaces — capabilities/next/graph/explain/search answer within interactive budgets on a fixture box, with a perf harness that catches regressions.

BACKGROUND: the brain is positioned as the read-FIRST surface for every new agent session (AGENTS.md core commands); if it dawdles, agents route around it and the investment dies. Adapters are already bounded (br 1.5s, bv 2.5s...), but nothing budgets the brain's own model-build + graph-build + ranking path, and nothing measures it over time. tests/perf/pulse_proof.py establishes the repo's pattern for in-memory perf proofs.

REASONING: performance is a feature of trust here: `next --no-adapters` must feel instant; with adapters it must be predictably bounded by the slowest adapter, not by accidental O(n^2) graph work.

IMPLEMENTATION CONSIDERATIONS: (1) tests/perf/brain_proof.py mirroring pulse_proof.py: build a representative fixture model (scaled: ~50 services/tasks/skills, ~500 graph nodes), then measure N iterations of each surface via the payload functions directly (not subprocess — measure compute, not python startup); assert budgets: capabilities <50ms, graph build+algorithm <150ms, next --no-adapters <150ms, search <100ms (calibrate on CI hardware first, set with 3x headroom, document the calibration run). (2) Add elapsed_ms to each brain payload's meta (cheap, permanent observability — agents and snapshots see cost). (3) Profile once during this bead (cProfile on the fixture); fix only egregious hotspots found (e.g. repeated model rebuilds per command — audit whether capabilities/next/graph share a cached model build within one process invocation; if each CLI call rebuilds, that is fine — but within one call, build once). (4) Subprocess-level smoke: one test asserting end-to-end `manage.py capabilities --no-adapters --format json` wall time < 2s (generous; catches import explosions).

FILES: tests/perf/brain_proof.py (new), runtime_manager payload functions (elapsed_ms meta), possibly caching in cli dispatch, docs (AGENTS.md note on budgets).

RISKS: flaky CI timing (run perf proof outside default discover like pulse_proof, or use generous multipliers + retry-once); budgets ossifying as the model grows (budgets scale with fixture, documented as fixture-relative).

ACCEPTANCE: (1) brain_proof runs standalone printing a table (surface, p50, p95, budget, PASS/FAIL); (2) all surfaces within budget on the fixture; (3) elapsed_ms present in payload meta (goldens regen once); (4) import-time smoke under 2s; (5) any hotspot fixes individually measured in the PR.

TESTING: the harness is the test; meta-field unit tests.

OBSERVABILITY: elapsed_ms in every brain payload; perf table in proof output.

MAINTAINER NOTES: This bead sets the bar, not the ceiling — future graph algorithms must run inside the same budget or declare themselves slow-class in the algorithm registry (cross-link: graph-algorithm-registry bead).
close_reason: Completed

title: MCP skill-content resources prototype (skillbox://skills/...)
description:
OBJECTIVE: Prototype the MCP resource layer for skill content — skillbox://skills/<name> resources served read-only by the in-box MCP server — implementing the local-mediation architecture that won the distribution duel (R1, scored 872/934 against remote live-fetch).

BACKGROUND: DUELING_WIZARDS_REPORT_R1 (distribution-phase1) converged on rejecting remote live skill fetch (violates VISION explicitness/privacy/low-ceremony) in favor of LOCAL skill runtime mediation: the box serves its own installed skill content over MCP resources/list + resources/read, enabling future stub-SKILL.md installs, usage telemetry, and content-on-demand without network dependency or trust changes. Estimated 300-500 lines; explicitly staged as prototype-first, with stub-SKILL.md-as-default DEFERRED until this layer proves reliable.

REASONING: today agents read skills from disk paths baked into homes — works, but invisible (no usage signal for Forge) and rigid (full copies everywhere). Resource mediation keeps content local + lockfile-backed (Design Stance #5) while making access observable and addressable.

IMPLEMENTATION CONSIDERATIONS: (1) .env-manager/mcp_server.py: implement resources/list (enumerate installed skills for the active scope from the skill-visibility layer — reuse collect_skill_visibility, do not re-walk disk) returning uri skillbox://skills/<name>, title, mimeType text/markdown; resources/read returning SKILL.md content (and bundled reference files as skillbox://skills/<name>/<relpath>, path-traversal-guarded). (2) Flag-gated: SKILLBOX_MCP_SKILL_RESOURCES=1, default OFF for the prototype release. (3) Event logging: every read appends {ts, skill, uri, session?} to a usage log under the state root — this is the Forge signal feed mentioned in the duel. (4) Read-only forever at this layer; no write/update resources. (5) Honor redaction module on served content? NO — skills are operator-authored content, serve verbatim; but enforce scope (only skills visible to the active client scope are listed/readable). (6) Protocol: resources are in MCP 2024-11-05 — the hand-rolled server needs the two new methods + capability advertisement; keep parity with its existing dispatch style.

FILES: .env-manager/mcp_server.py, runtime_manager/skill_visibility.py (lookup helper), .env.example (flag), tests/test_mcp_server*.py, docs (README MCP section).

RISKS: hand-rolled protocol drift (pin against the spec section in comments; contract tests with raw JSON-RPC fixtures); large bundled assets (cap resource size, return a pointer-style message over the cap); scope leaks (client-scoped visibility must gate the list — test it).

ACCEPTANCE: (1) with flag on, resources/list returns exactly the active scope's skills; (2) resources/read round-trips SKILL.md bytes; (3) traversal attempts (skillbox://skills/../../etc) rejected; (4) flag off -> capability not advertised, methods return method-not-found; (5) usage log lines on every read; (6) duel report linked from the code comment.

TESTING: JSON-RPC fixture tests for both methods + capability negotiation; scope-gating test (client A cannot list client B's skills); traversal tests; flag-off tests.

OBSERVABILITY: the usage log (feeds Forge later); list/read counts could surface in evidence as a stretch.

MAINTAINER NOTES: This is deliberately a PROTOTYPE: ship behind the flag, dogfood, THEN file the stub-SKILL.md bead if telemetry proves reliability — that ordering was the duel's explicit verdict. Do not skip to stubs.
close_reason: done

title: Generate docs/API_REFERENCE.md from the command registry + freshness check
description:
OBJECTIVE: Auto-generate docs/API_REFERENCE.md from the command registry — every command's tier, surfaces, inputs/outputs, side-effect class, risk, scopes, examples, and MCP mirror — with a freshness check so it can never drift.

BACKGROUND: command_registry.py is a complete machine-readable ABI (CommandSpec carries summary, input/output schemas, side_effect, risk, entrypoint, examples, mcp_tool, scopes, validations) validated by REQUIRED_TIER1/TIER2 completeness checks — but the only human/agent-readable rendering is scattered README tables maintained by hand (the 2,231-line README documents ~30 commands in prose tables that already lag the registry). The docs audit flagged the missing API reference explicitly.

REASONING: the registry was BUILT to be the single source of truth; rendering it closes the loop — one new CommandSpec automatically produces correct docs, capabilities payload, and (post cli-split) dispatch checks. Agents browsing the repo (or the web) get the same contract the brain serves.

IMPLEMENTATION CONSIDERATIONS: (1) New command `manage.py registry-docs --format md` (register it in the registry too — pleasingly self-hosting; tier 2, side_effect none... but --write writes the file: model it like snap, print by default, --write to emit docs/API_REFERENCE.md). (2) Rendering: grouped by tier then domain prefix (brain.*, runtime.*, outer.*, box.*, make.*); per command: summary, surfaces, scopes, side_effect/risk badges, input/output schema tables (flatten the JSON-Schema-ish dicts to name/type/required rows), examples as fenced blocks, MCP mirror name, validation commands. Deterministic output (sorted, no timestamps beyond a generated-from line with REGISTRY_ABI_VERSION). (3) Freshness: a unit test renders in-memory and diffs against the committed file — same pattern as context drift goldens (REGEN env var to rewrite); CI thus fails when someone edits the registry without regenerating. (4) README's command tables get a pointer to the reference (actual README slimming is the README-restructure bead's job — coordinate, do not double-edit).

FILES: runtime_manager (renderer module + cli registration), command_registry.py (self-entry), docs/API_REFERENCE.md (generated), tests/test_registry_docs.py (new).

RISKS: schema dicts too irregular to table-render (fallback: fenced JSON for complex schemas — better honest JSON than mangled tables); merge conflicts on the generated file (regeneration is deterministic; conflicts resolve by regenerating).

ACCEPTANCE: (1) registry-docs output deterministic across runs; (2) docs/API_REFERENCE.md committed and covers every registry entry (count assertion); (3) freshness test fails on a planted registry edit without regen; (4) the file renders cleanly on GitHub (manual check noted in PR); (5) registry-docs itself appears in the reference.

TESTING: determinism test (two renders byte-equal); coverage-count test; freshness drift test; golden for one representative command's section.

OBSERVABILITY: generated-from header with ABI version.

MAINTAINER NOTES: Never hand-edit API_REFERENCE.md (header says so). If the rendering is wrong, fix the renderer; if the content is wrong, fix the registry — that division is the whole point.
close_reason: Generated command registry API reference, CLI command, freshness tests, and README pointer.

title: Adopt unified error envelope across brain surfaces + MCP mirrors
description:
OBJECTIVE: Adopt the unified error envelope (from the typed-contracts epic) across all six brain surfaces — capabilities, next, graph, explain, search, snap — and their MCP mirrors, so brain errors are as machine-stable as brain successes.

BACKGROUND: the error-hierarchy bead establishes SkillboxError + envelope and adopts it in lifecycle surfaces (doctor/sync/up/down) as the exemplar. Brain surfaces currently raise/format errors ad hoc (UNKNOWN_NODE payloads, argparse failures, adapter degradations are each shaped differently). The fuzzy-suggestions bead enriches UNKNOWN_NODE; this bead standardizes the carrier so suggestions/next_actions live in the same place on EVERY brain error.

REASONING: agents script against the brain first; its error envelope consistency pays the highest rent. Splitting adoption from definition keeps both PRs reviewable and lets lifecycle adoption shake out envelope design flaws before the brain commits.

IMPLEMENTATION CONSIDERATIONS: (1) Convert each brain surface's failure paths to raise the typed errors: UNKNOWN_NODE/AMBIGUOUS_NODE (explain), UNKNOWN_ALGORITHM (graph), SNAPSHOT_NOT_FOUND/SNAPSHOT_SCHEMA_MISMATCH (snap), SEARCH_INDEX_EMPTY (search, if applicable), adapter-degradation notes stay non-fatal (they are warnings in success payloads, NOT errors — preserve that). (2) MCP mirrors map the envelope into MCP error content consistently (one mapping function shared with lifecycle adoption). (3) Suggestions/resolved_from fields from the fuzzy bead ride in error.context — align field names with that bead (coordinate; whichever lands second conforms). (4) Goldens: one deliberate regeneration; snapshot replay fixtures may embed old error shapes — regenerate tests/goldens/agent_ops_snapshot.json via the documented flow.

FILES: agent_decisions.py, agent_graph_engine.py, agent_search.py, agent_snapshots.py, cli brain handlers, mcp_server.py, goldens, tests.

RISKS: consumers (sbp launch? evidence packet?) parsing current brain error shapes — grep consumers for the legacy keys first and keep the dual-emit window consistent with the lifecycle bead's deprecation schedule.

ACCEPTANCE: (1) every brain failure mode emits the envelope (enumerated test matrix per surface); (2) MCP mirror parity test (same code, same envelope, MCP framing); (3) adapter degradations remain warnings in success payloads; (4) goldens regenerated once; (5) dual-emit window matches lifecycle surfaces.

TESTING: per-surface failure matrix; MCP parity tests; golden regen; consumer grep audit recorded in PR.

OBSERVABILITY: envelopes; error-code counts visible in evidence stretch (see error-hierarchy bead).

MAINTAINER NOTES: After this bead, envelope adoption order for remaining surfaces (clients, reports, forge, workers) is maintainer's discretion — file follow-on beads per domain as touched; do not big-bang them.
close_reason: Completed

title: Run agent-ergonomics skill on Skillbox agent-facing CLI surfaces
description:
NO-RAGRETS CONTRACT
Outcome: Skillbox's agent-facing CLI surfaces get a real agent-ergonomics pass, not ad hoc polish, before the agent-ergonomics epic is considered done.
Evidence: an in-tree agent_ergonomics_audit/ workspace exists with surface inventory, scorecard, recommendations, applied_changes or explicit audit-only rationale, regression tests for accepted changes, and before/after command transcripts.
Failure avoided: future agents improve one or two obvious commands but miss systemic CLI usability failures around json/robot modes, error pedagogy, intent recovery, stdout/stderr separation, deterministic output, and self-documentation.

SKILL TO RUN
Use agent-ergonomics-and-intuitiveness-maximization-for-cli-tools. Start with that skill's required progress marker and read its SKILL.md before work. Target this repo's agent-facing CLIs and MCP mirrors, especially:
- python3 .env-manager/manage.py capabilities/next/graph/explain/search/snap and registered runtime commands
- scripts/04-reconcile.py render/doctor robot-help and json/robot aliases
- scripts/box.py json/dry-run/error surfaces that agents call through make targets and MCP
- scripts/sbp if this pass is being run from the sbp wrapper workstream

PLACEMENT AND SCOPE
This belongs under skillbox-agent-ergonomics-epic-086q. Run full mode unless the operator explicitly asks for audit-only. Keep the audit workspace in-tree at /srv/skillbox/repos/opensource/skillbox/agent_ergonomics_audit/. Do not create a branch or sibling workspace. Do not bundle new product features into the ergonomics pass; file separate beads for feature-sized gaps.

ACCEPTANCE
1. phase0 preflight records target path, mode, current branch, toolchain status, helper-skill availability, and scope guardrails.
2. The pass scores the relevant CLI surfaces across the 11 dimensions with evidence for high scores and ranks the top fixes.
3. Accepted fixes include regression tests or golden/snapshot coverage that fails if the ergonomic behavior regresses.
4. The pass verifies at least the focused commands plus the relevant focused tests; broaden to python3 -m unittest discover -s tests when practical.
5. HANDOFF.md or equivalent Beads comments list deferred recommendations with bead IDs.

VALIDATION COMMANDS
- python3 .env-manager/manage.py capabilities --format json
- python3 .env-manager/manage.py next --format json
- python3 .env-manager/manage.py graph --format json

title: Investigate profile-resolution inconsistency across up / ingress-sync / exposure
description:
Before building the aggregate, explain a contradiction observed on 2026-06-04: 'sbp up' from haas repo STARTED haas-web (so the up path resolved haas-web under local-frontend/local-all), yet 'render --client haas' resolved 0 ingress_routes (haas route gated to local-all but default render used active profile 'core'), AND the up output reported haas-web at http://localhost:9080 loopback-only even though SKILLBOX_INGRESS_PRIVATE_BASE_URL is the Tailnet IP and the on-disk manifest's private base_url is the Tailnet IP.

TASK: trace the exact model-resolution path used by (a) _up_ordered_services service start, (b) sync_ingress_artifacts manifest write, and (c) service_endpoint_exposure (endpoints.py) reporting. Determine which profile each uses and why exposure computed localhost rather than the Tailnet base_url. Document findings in the bead.

WHY IT MATTERS: the aggregate builder and the persistent-profile work depend on profile resolution being consistent and predictable. If service start and manifest generation disagree on the active profile/route set, the aggregate will be wrong.

SUCCESS: written explanation of the resolution path + identified root cause(s); note any bugs to fix as their own beads.
close_reason: Root-cause trace documented in comment 48. The route/service mismatch is explained by direct manage.py defaulting to core-only while sbp runtime commands default to local-all with cwd-based client inference. Manifest sync and service start use the same filtered model; current sbp up dry-run/status report ingress-routed, so the older loopback-only output is not reproducible. Existing children cover persistent local-all, aggregate manifest, and MagicDNS/base-url follow-ups.

comments.author: skillbox
comments.text:
Trace result 2026-06-04:

1. Direct manage.py model commands filter once in cli._filtered_model_for_args. normalize_active_profiles([]) adds only core. Therefore python3 .env-manager/manage.py render --client haas --format json produces active_profiles=[core], includes the haas client/repo/log, but excludes haas-web and haas-private-root because both are profile-gated to local-frontend/local-all.

2. The sbp wrapper is not equivalent to direct render defaults. scripts/sbp defaults profile=local-all and passes --cwd <invoke_cwd> when no client is explicit. From haas repo, scripts/sbp up --dry-run --json resolves client haas, active_profiles=[core, local-all], includes ingress-router, haas-web, haas-install, and haas-private-root.

3. Local up path: cli._handle_up detects local_runtime_active_profile(model), then cli._handle_local_profile_up calls workflows.run_up(model, profile=local-all). workflows.run_up computes _up_ordered_services from that already-filtered model, runs bootstrap, then calls sync_ingress_artifacts(model) before start_services. sync_ingress_artifacts renders exactly the current filtered model via render_ingress_routes_document(model); there is no separate profile selection in the manifest write.

4. Endpoint exposure path: runtime_status and _emit_up_payload both pass box_access into endpoints.annotate_service_rows. service_endpoint_exposure finds routes from model.ingress_routes, builds private listener request_url from SKILLBOX_INGRESS_PRIVATE_BASE_URL when present, and converts wildcard listener host <wildcard-host> to a tailnet_url using runtime_box_access_from_env. Current exact wrapper dry-run and status both report haas-web exposure=ingress-routed with access_url/tailnet_url http://<tailnet-host>:9080/.

5. Current root cause: the observed 0-route render was due to using direct manage.py render without --profile local-all, while sbp runtime commands default to local-all. This is profile-selection mismatch, not a separate service-start vs manifest-generation model path. The older loopback-only up output is not reproducible on current code/config; current sbp up dry-run and sbp status report ingress-routed.

Existing follow-up coverage: child .15 tracks making local-all persistent/default for the box posture, .8 tracks single-client manifest overwrite vs aggregate build, and .9 tracks replacing the hardcoded Tailnet IP with MagicDNS/box_access derivation. No new bug bead is needed from this trace.

title: Architectural wall: multi-tier apps (spaps loopback-by-design) resist Tailnet exposure
description:
Port-per-app direct Tailnet bind works cleanly for SINGLE-process frontends (9 done: haas,raas,buildooor,cca,sweet-potato-docs,mhb,unclawg,design-system-registry,inschneidergram).

It does NOT cleanly work for MULTI-TIER apps:
 - spaps (auth tier for finalreceipts, htma, sweet-potato, cycle-chef scenes) is LOOPBACK-BY-DESIGN: src hardcodes localhost/localhost (home-view.js, local-runtime.js, fixture-kernel.js; binds localhost). It is a local dev auth mock; serving it on the tailnet fights its design and exposes a dev shim.
 - Frontends bake localhost API URLs into client bundles (finalreceipts PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL/PUBLIC_SPAPS_API_URL; cycle-chef/htma VITE_API_URL=localhost:8000). From a phone these resolve to the phone itself -> broken.
 - Backends (ingredient_server:8001, htma_server:8000) bind localhost and are shared/duplicated across scene clients (cannot coexist).

DECISION NEEDED (3 options): 
 (A) Front multi-tier apps with the Tailnet ingress (the originally-deprioritized reverse proxy) so apps stay loopback and the proxy exposes them — but spaps localhost Host-header checks may still reject; needs testing.
 (B) Refactor: make backends+spaps tailnet-capable + rebuild frontends with tailnet API URLs (large, multi-repo, fights spaps design).
 (C) Accept multi-tier apps as loopback-only on the box (functioning locally, not phone-viewable) and treat only single-process frontends as phone-reachable.

Recommendation: (A) for viewing + (C) as the honest default; (B) only if a scene app must be fully phone-interactive.
close_reason: Decision recorded: direct Tailnet ports are the phone-viewable contract for selected single-process web apps. Multi-tier scene stacks with loopback-baked frontend API URLs or loopback-only auth/backend shims stay local-box workflows for now. A dedicated Tailnet proxy or multi-repo backend/auth refactor remains future explicit work, not part of the current rollout.

comments.text:
Spike findings 2026-06-04:

Setup:
- Backed up .skillbox-state/logs/runtime/ingress-routes.json to /tmp/skillbox-ingress-routes.before-haas-spike.json.
- Temporarily added private prefix route id=haas-private-prefix-spike path=/haas match=prefix service_id=haas-web origin_url=http://<tailnet-host>:8787.
- Restored the original generated manifest after probes; ingress health returned to private route count 7.

Runtime state observed:
- haas-web is running under local-all and Wrangler is bound to http://<tailnet-host>:8787.
- http://localhost:8787/ is not reachable, so the spike used the live Tailnet-bound origin rather than loopback.
- Existing generated manifest did not include haas and already contained several private '/' prefix routes from other clients, confirming the current aggregate/root-collision risk.

Command-first evidence:
- Direct origin GET / -> 200, 24544 bytes.
- Direct origin GET /styles.css -> 200, 18138 bytes.
- Direct origin GET /app.js -> 200, 1120 bytes.
- Direct origin GET /config.js -> 200, 246 bytes.
- Ingress GET http://localhost:9080/haas -> 404, 0 bytes.
- Ingress GET http://localhost:9080/haas/ -> 404, 0 bytes.
- Ingress GET http://localhost:9080/haas/styles.css -> 404, 0 bytes.
- Tailnet ingress GET http://<tailnet-host>:9080/haas -> 404, 0 bytes.
- Tailnet ingress GET http://<tailnet-host>:9080/haas/styles.css -> 404, 0 bytes.
- haas Wrangler logs show GET /haas, /haas/, /haas/styles.css, and /haas/app.js all reached the origin and returned 404. This confirms the proxy forwards the original prefixed path and does not strip.

What breaks:
1. The document route itself breaks under path-prefix routing because Wrangler/ASSETS does not serve /haas or /haas/.
2. public/index.html uses absolute root asset URLs: /config.js, /app.js, /styles.css.
3. public/index.html also uses a root home link href=/. At /haas, that navigates back to the ingress root rather than the app prefix.
4. A future strip_prefix=true would make /haas load /, and /haas/styles.css load /styles.css if the browser requested prefixed assets. It would not by itself fix the current HTML, because absolute /config.js, /app.js, and /styles.css requests would still target the ingress root.

Follow-up needed for child .11:
- Update haas public/index.html to use a configurable base path or prefixed/relative assets for config.js, app.js, and styles.css.
- Update the home link/router assumptions so the app stays under /haas.
- Update src/worker.ts so /haas/config.js and/or a configured base path map to the runtime config response, or make the HTML request a relative config path that resolves under the prefix.
- Keep optional strip_prefix as an API/path-agnostic helper only; haas still needs base-path work for static assets and navigation.

title: Make overlay dry-run non-mutating end to end
description:
## Finding
`python3 .env-manager/manage.py overlay on <name> --dry-run --format json` writes persistent overlay state anyway, and `scripts/sbp overlay ... --dry-run` follows by running `skill sync` without `--dry-run`.

## Affected paths
- .env-manager/runtime_manager/cli.py:2906-3032
- .env-manager/runtime_manager/skill_visibility.py:466-483,521-562
- scripts/sbp:876-880
- tests/test_skill_visibility.py
- tests/test_cli_wrappers.py

## Root cause
`_handle_overlay` calls `_apply_persistent_overlay_action` and `_overlay_removed_links` before considering `args.dry_run`; the wrapper does not propagate dry-run to the follow-up policy sync.

## Describe / reproduce contract
Given `SKILLBOX_OVERLAY_STATE` points at an empty temp path, when `overlay on audit-dryrun --dry-run --format json` runs, then the state file must not be created and JSON must describe planned state without claiming persistence. Given `sbp overlay marketing --dry-run`, when it reaches policy sync, then any follow-up `skill sync` must be skipped or run with `--dry-run`.

## Validation commands
- `python3 -m unittest tests.test_skill_visibility tests.test_cli_wrappers`
- `tmp=$(mktemp -d); SKILLBOX_OVERLAY_STATE="$tmp/overlays" python3 .env-manager/manage.py overlay on audit-dryrun --dry-run --format json; test ! -e "$tmp/overlays"`
- `git diff --check`

## Closeout evidence
Show the focused tests and temp-state probe passing. Do not touch unrelated overlay policy.
close_reason: Overlay dry-run is non-mutating end to end; focused tests, temp-state probe, diff check, and dependency cycle check passed.

title: Enforce runtime MCP dry-run-first for mutating tools
description:
## Finding
The runtime MCP server advertises dry-run-first for mutating tools, but `dispatch_tool` calls `manage.py` directly when `dry_run` is omitted. Confirmed for `skillbox_sync`, `skillbox_up`, `skillbox_down`, `skillbox_restart`, `skillbox_bootstrap`, and `skillbox_onboard`.

## Affected paths
- .env-manager/mcp_server.py:682-832,1416-1479,1487-1521,1696-1720
- tests/test_mcp_server.py

## Root cause
Tool metadata and initialize instructions encode the safety rule as prose, not as dispatcher policy. `_dispatch_manage_tool` validates identifiers and required positionals, then always calls `run_manage`.

## Describe / pass-fail contract
Given a mutating MCP tool with `dry_run_required` semantics, when the tool is called without `dry_run=true`, then the MCP response must be `isError=true` with a structured `dry_run_required` error and `run_manage` must not be called. Given the same tool with `dry_run=true`, when it succeeds, then the preview response should include enough subject/marker context to allow the corresponding real action if that command is intentionally allowed.

## Validation commands
- `python3 -m unittest tests.test_mcp_server`
- No-side-effect monkeypatch proof: dispatch each mutating tool without dry_run and assert `run_manage` was not invoked.
- `git diff --check`

## Closeout evidence
Show tests for missing dry-run, allowed dry-run, and at least one scoped real-action policy if implemented. Keep read-only tools unaffected.
close_reason: Runtime MCP dry-run-first enforcement implemented with matching marker tests; focused MCP tests, diff check, and dependency cycle check passed.

title: Return nonzero when legacy up or restart service starts fail
description:
## Finding
Legacy `up` and `restart` paths return `EXIT_OK` even when `start_services(...)` returns entries with `result: failed`, `timeout`, or `blocked`. Local-runtime profiles already classify these failures in `workflows._up_services_payload`.

## Affected paths
- .env-manager/runtime_manager/cli.py:3195-3244,3269-3312
- .env-manager/runtime_manager/workflows.py:3912-3980
- tests/test_runtime_manager.py or focused CLI unit tests

## Root cause
The legacy path packages raw `service_results` and hardcodes `EXIT_OK` in `_handle_up` and `_handle_restart`; it never maps unhealthy service result values into an error envelope or nonzero exit.

## Describe / reproduce contract
Given `start_services` returns `[{"id":"svc","result":"failed"}]`, when legacy `_handle_up(... --format json)` runs, then it must return `EXIT_ERROR` and emit a structured error naming the failed service. Given all service starts are `started` or `already-running`, the existing success output and exit 0 must remain unchanged. Apply the same rule to restart start results.

## Validation commands
- `python3 -m unittest tests.test_runtime_manager tests.test_text_renderers`
- Add a no-side-effect unit test that monkeypatches `start_services` to return `failed` and asserts nonzero.
- `git diff --check`

## Closeout evidence
Show failing-service and success-regression tests. Keep local-profile `LOCAL_RUNTIME_START_BLOCKED` behavior aligned rather than duplicating a divergent error shape.
close_reason: Legacy up/restart now return LOCAL_RUNTIME_START_BLOCKED on failed, timeout, or blocked starts; focused and broad runtime tests passed.

title: Guard install.sh --force against dangerous target deletion
description:
## Finding
`install.sh --force` runs `rm -rf` on the resolved `--repo-dir` if it exists and is non-empty, with no denylist for `/`, `$HOME`, repo parents, or non-Skillbox directories.

## Affected paths
- install.sh:361-367,620-664,1182-1230
- tests/test_install_script.py

## Root cause
`ensure_checkout_target_ready` treats every user-supplied target as disposable once `--force` is set. It does not require a Skillbox sentinel, a safe install-root shape, or a backup/rename path before deletion.

## Describe / pass-fail contract
Given `--repo-dir /`, `$HOME`, the current repo parent, or a non-Skillbox temp directory containing a sentinel file, when install runs with `--force`, then it must exit nonzero and leave the sentinel untouched. Given an existing Skillbox checkout target with `.env-manager/manage.py` and `--force`, then replacement remains possible through a safer backup/rename flow or an explicit approved path.

## Validation commands
- `python3 -m unittest tests.test_install_script`
- `bash -n install.sh`
- `git diff --check`

## Closeout evidence
Show destructive-target regression tests that prove user data is preserved. Avoid broad installer rewrites outside target safety.

title: Harden binary push script shell and remote-command quoting
description:

`scripts/07-build-and-push-binary.sh` interpolates `SKILLBOX_BUILD_APT_DEPS`, `PKG`, `BIN_NAME`, `TARGET_BIN_DIR`, and `SYMLINK_DIR` into local `bash -c` and remote SSH shell strings, then uses privileged Docker on the target to write symlinks.

title: Make worker-submit return durable queued/running state instead of blocking on Hermes
description:
## Finding
`worker-submit` is documented as a brokered worker surface, but `create_worker_run` calls Hermes with blocking `subprocess.run(...)` inside submit. The default launch timeout is 300s, so a long or hung worker can tie up the CLI/MCP request and be classified as launch failure rather than a durable running job.

## Affected paths
- .env-manager/runtime_manager/shared.py:1238-1312,1315-1441
- .env-manager/runtime_manager/cli.py worker-submit/status handlers
- tests/test_worker_runtime.py

## Root cause
The submit path persists `worker.launching`, then synchronously waits for Hermes to finish and immediately loads terminal result files. There is no PID/heartbeat-running state for `worker-status` to reconcile.

## Describe / pass-fail contract
Given Hermes starts successfully but does not finish immediately, when `worker-submit` is called, then it should return quickly with a durable `queued` or `running` state and a run id. Given the worker later writes `result.json`, when `worker-status <run_id>` runs, then it should reconcile to the terminal result and expose artifacts. Given Hermes cannot start, launch failure should remain structured and immediate.

## Validation commands
- `python3 -m unittest tests.test_worker_runtime`
- Add a fake long-running Hermes test that proves submit returns before timeout and status can later reconcile.
- `git diff --check`

## Closeout evidence
Show async submit/status tests and preserve existing immediate-failure behavior. Keep learning-promotion review gates unchanged.
close_reason: worker-submit now returns durable running state and status reconciles terminal Hermes results; focused/full worker tests passed

title: Lube: cass-lube-scout prompt should skip rebuild since mirror-sync cron keeps index fresh
description:
CASS evidence: 283 hits for 'cass index stale run rebuild', 477 for 'sbp cass rebuild'. The cass-lube-scout.sh prompt tells agents to 'run sbp cass rebuild and wait for it to finish' when the index is stale. But the cass-mirror-sync.sh cron runs every 30 minutes and keeps the index fresh. A full rebuild (rclone sync + projection + reindex) takes 30-40 minutes and blocks the scout for its entire runtime.

Observed directly in this session: sbp cass status was stale, but the index had 232K matches and was fully searchable. The mirror-sync cron had already refreshed it. Running a full rebuild was unnecessary — the scout just needed the index to be queryable, which it was.

No-ragrets success contract:
- Outcome: cass-lube-scout.sh prompt checks status, proceeds with mining if the index is queryable (health OK or degraded with matches), and only blocks on rebuild if the index is completely empty/broken.
- Evidence: this session wasted minutes on rebuild when the index was already usable. 283 sessions hit the same rebuild ceremony.
- Failure avoided: scout sessions burning 30+ minutes on unnecessary rebuilds when the cron already maintains freshness.
- Acceptance: (1) scout checks sbp cass status, (2) proceeds if probe shows matches, (3) only runs rebuild if zero matches or error, (4) cron keeps index fresh between scouts.
close_reason: Fix applied: updated cass-lube-scout.sh prompt to check status and proceed if probe has matches, only rebuild on zero matches/error. Uses --skip-archive-upload to avoid unnecessary R2 upload step.

title: Durable-state backup & restore drill
description:
EPIC: Give the durable state a real continuity story: first-class backup tooling for .skillbox-state plus a restore drill that converts the stewardship report's standing "not_assessed" verdict on backup/restore into dated evidence.

WHY: skillbox's core thesis is durable state (Design Stance #2) — agent homes, client overlays, logs, monoserver repos all live under SKILLBOX_STATE_ROOT — yet the project ships ZERO backup tooling and stewardship-report explicitly marks backup/restore drills as not_assessed (README: "important hardening domains that are not yet proven"). A box that remembers everything until the first disk failure remembers nothing.

SCOPE BOUNDARY: operator-grade local backup + verified restore. NOT in scope: offsite replication, scheduling/retention policy automation, encryption-at-rest (the state root may contain secrets — backups inherit that posture and the docs say so loudly; offsite/encryption are follow-up decisions once the primitive exists).

EXIT: one command produces a verifiable backup; one command proves a backup restores; stewardship cites the latest drill with a date instead of not_assessed.
close_reason: done

title: state-backup create/list/verify with checksummed manifest
description:
OBJECTIVE: Implement `manage.py state-backup create|list|verify` — tar.gz snapshots of SKILLBOX_STATE_ROOT with a checksummed manifest — as a registered, structured-output command.

BACKGROUND: .skillbox-state holds everything the box's durability promise covers: clients/, home/.claude + .codex (agent memory, skills, sessions), logs/, monoserver/ (potentially large repo checkouts). Today the operator's only option is ad-hoc tar — no manifest, no verification, no exclusion intelligence, no integration with doctor/stewardship.

REASONING: backup needs to be one boring command or it will not happen; making it a registry command gives it MCP visibility, capabilities listing, and the standard payload contract for free.

IMPLEMENTATION CONSIDERATIONS: (1) create: stream a tar.gz of the state root to ${SKILLBOX_BACKUP_ROOT:-<state-root-sibling>/skillbox-backups}/skillbox-state-<utc-stamp>.tar.gz — destination must be OUTSIDE the state root (no recursive backups) and validated against being inside it; write alongside it a manifest json {created_at, source_root, file_count, total_bytes, sha256 (of the tarball), tool_version, excludes_applied, top_level_entries:[{path, bytes}]}. (2) Default excludes (overridable --include-all): caches and reproducibles — monoserver/ (repos re-clone; INCLUDE by flag --with-monoserver), logs/ older than N days? NO — keep logs, they are the box's memory; exclude only known cache dirs (pruned-skill-repo-extras-*, rch-adapter caches, __pycache__) — the exclude table is explicit in code with a comment per entry. (3) verify: recompute tarball sha256 against manifest + structural spot-check (tar -t parses, manifest top_level_entries present). (4) list: table of backups with age/size/verified-status. (5) Registry: tier 2, side_effect local_write, risk low; MCP mirror skillbox_state_backup gated behind the dry-run-first discipline? create is additive (never overwrites) — plain call acceptable, document why. (6) Secrets: the tarball contains agent homes (tokens in ~/.claude etc.) — manifest and docs state this in bold; backups land mode 0600. title: state-backup drill + guarded restore + stewardship evidence integration
description:
OBJECTIVE: Implement `state-backup drill` (restore-to-temp + structural validation) and an in-place `state-backup restore` with heavy guardrails, then wire drill evidence into stewardship-report so backup/restore flips from not_assessed to dated assessment.

BACKGROUND: a backup nobody has restored is a hope, not a backup. stewardship-report (README: marks "backup/restore drills and cost review as not_assessed") already models exactly this gap — the drill closes the loop: prove restorability mechanically, on a schedule the operator controls, with evidence the reporting surface consumes.

REASONING: the drill-to-temp design makes proving restore SAFE (no production state touched), so it can run casually — which is the only way it runs at all.

IMPLEMENTATION CONSIDERATIONS: (1) drill: pick newest (or --backup <path>) verified backup -> extract to a temp dir -> structural validation: expected top-level entries present (vs manifest), key invariants hold (clients/*/overlay.yaml parse as YAML, home/.claude exists, skill lockfiles parse, no path escapes during extraction — use tarfile filter='data' (py3.12+) / equivalent safe-extract for older), file count within tolerance of manifest -> write drill evidence json under the state root ({ts, backup_path, sha256, checks:[...], ok}) -> clean up temp (keep on --keep for inspection). (2) restore (in-place): REQUIRES --i-understand-data-loss flag + an automatic safety backup of current state FIRST (reuse create) + refuses while pulse is running (pid check) + refuses on sha256 mismatch; restores to a staging sibling then swaps (atomic-ish via rename dance documented honestly); this is the one command in the plan that can destroy state — its test coverage and its guardrails are the bulk of the work. (3) stewardship-report: read latest drill evidence; backup/restore domain shows {last_drill, age_days, ok} and reverts to not_assessed when age > 30d (configurable) — the audit surface drives the habit. (4) Registry entries; MCP mirrors restore NOT exposed over MCP (operator-terminal-only, documented why: destructive + interactive confidence required).

FILES: runtime_manager/state_backup.py (extend), stewardship report module, cli/registry, tests, docs.

RISKS: unsafe tar extraction (use the stdlib data filter; explicit test with a malicious member fixture); restore swap failing midway (the pre-restore safety backup is the recovery; the swap procedure logs each step so a manual unwind is scriptable); drill temp space (same free-space pre-check as create).

ACCEPTANCE: (1) drill on a healthy backup passes all checks and writes evidence; (2) drill on a corrupted backup fails naming the failed check; (3) malicious-member tarball is neutralized (test); (4) restore refuses without the flag, with pulse running, and on checksum mismatch; (5) restore round-trip on a fixture (create -> mutate -> restore -> state equals original) passes; (6) stewardship shows the dated drill and decays to not_assessed past the window.

TESTING: as above plus stewardship integration test with planted evidence files of varying ages.

OBSERVABILITY: drill evidence json is the artifact; runtime.log lines for drill/restore start+outcome; restore prints a step-by-step transcript.

MAINTAINER NOTES: The not_assessed decay is the feature that keeps this honest forever — resist making evidence permanent. If the operator stops drilling, the report should start nagging again.

title: Fix runtime defects: zombie liveness, cwd-inference re-sort, durable session ordering
description:
Random-fix pass found and fixed three real defects plus stale tests after the recent sbp/box work.

comments.author: claude-opus
comments.text:
## BoxNetworkPosture Contract — Implementation Evidence

### Fields Added to Box Dataclass (scripts/box.py)

- `network_posture: str = ""` — desired posture. Valid values: `tailnet_only`, `public`, `unmanaged`. Empty string is the migration default for old inventory.
- `cloud_firewall_id: str | None = None` — optional reference to a cloud provider firewall (e.g. DigitalOcean firewall ID).

### Posture Constants

- `POSTURE_TAILNET_ONLY = "tailnet_only"` — SSH restricted to Tailnet CIDR, cloud firewall required, wildcard-direct app binds forbidden
- `POSTURE_PUBLIC = "public"` — public SSH allowed, no cloud firewall required, all app binds allowed
- `POSTURE_UNMANAGED = "unmanaged"` — no posture enforcement (for external/registered boxes)

### Migration Behavior

- `resolve_network_posture(box)` resolves empty/missing field to safe defaults:
  - Managed boxes (management_mode="managed") → tailnet_only
  - External boxes (management_mode="external") → unmanaged
- Old inventory without the field loads cleanly via existing `Box(**{k: v for ...})` pattern — unknown keys are filtered, new keys get dataclass defaults

### Policy Functions

- `posture_allows_public_ssh(posture)` — True only for "public"
- `posture_requires_cloud_firewall(posture)` — True only for "tailnet_only"
- `posture_requires_host_ssh_lockdown(posture)` — True only for "tailnet_only"
- `posture_allows_exposure(posture, exposure)` — False for wildcard-direct on tailnet_only, True for everything else

### Exposure Classification (Distinguished Bind Types)

- `wildcard-direct` — app binds 0.0.0.0, reachable on all interfaces (VIOLATION under tailnet_only)
- `tailnet-direct` — app binds Tailnet IP directly (allowed under tailnet_only)
- `ingress-routed` — app accessible via ingress proxy on Tailnet (allowed under tailnet_only)
- `loopback-only` — app binds localhost/127.x only (allowed under tailnet_only, not Tailnet-reachable)

### Policy-Failure Semantics

`evaluate_posture_violations(box, network_checks=..., app_exposures=...)` returns a list of violation dicts:
- `public_ssh_reachable` (severity: error) — SSH reachable on public IP under tailnet_only posture
- `cloud_firewall_missing` (severity: warning) — no cloud firewall ID under tailnet_only posture
- `app_exposure_violation` (severity: error) — wildcard-direct app bind under tailnet_only posture

Unmanaged boxes return no violations (no enforcement).

### Tests (24 passing)

- Old inventory loads without posture field, Box.network_posture defaults to ""
- Old managed box resolves to tailnet_only, old external resolves to unmanaged
- Explicit posture values are respected
- New managed Box defaults to tailnet_only
- All posture policy functions tested for each posture value
- Violation evaluator tested for SSH, cloud firewall, and app exposure scenarios
- Posture roundtrips through inventory save/load

title: Make br auto-inject read-only flags in non-TTY (agent) contexts
description:

title: Brain returns unsafe orientation: command injection, load-guard truncation, adapter argv echo
description:
The orientation quality baseline (skillbox-duel-brain-quality-lab-l5zt, commit 6bb6dbf) records 3 false-safe scenarios / 6 findings against the CURRENT brain. All three are real defects in agent_decisions.py, reproducible via 'python3 tests/quality/brain_orientation_proof.py'. Zero false-abstain.

1. COMMAND INJECTION (agent_decisions.py:362). _ready_work_recommendations interpolates the raw work-item id into 'br update {id} --status=in_progress' with NO id-grammar check. A work item whose id contains shell metacharacters turns the suggested command into a destructive one-liner, and the brain still ranks it TOP instead of abstaining. Proof scenario emits: 'br update orient-901; rm -rf ./PLACEHOLDER_SCRATCH --status=in_progress'. Fix: validate the id against a strict grammar and abstain (do not merely escape) when it fails.

2. ADAPTER ARGV ECHO (agent_decisions.py:328). _adapter_warning_recommendations echoes ' '.join(adapter['command']) verbatim into agent-facing 'commands', replaying whatever argv a degraded adapter recorded. Proof scenario emits: 'sh -c rm -rf ./PLACEHOLDER_SCRATCH && skills --issues'. Fix: never echo adapter-recorded argv into a suggested command; name the adapter and let the caller look it up.

3. LOAD GUARD TRUNCATED OUT (agent_decisions.py:483-511). 'respect-load-guard' scores 920 but a P0 bv-ranked 'claim-ready' scores 930, so at limit=1 the no-go load guard is silently dropped from the answer. limit=1 is the shape tests/perf/brain_proof.py uses for live observation AND the common MCP call, so in practice the guard is invisible exactly when it matters. Fix: cautions must not compete with actions for the same limited slots.

Acceptance: the three baseline scenarios flip to pass, the recorded baseline in tests/goldens/agent_ops_orientation_scenarios.json is deliberately updated, and 'brain_orientation_proof.py --strict' exits 0.
close_reason: Implemented in f8e6a06: id-grammar abstention, adapter argv withheld, cautions moved to an unsliced channel. Baseline 17/20 -> 20/20 with 0 false-safe and 0 false-abstain, --strict exit 0 re-verified; id grammar probed directly (rejects 'orient-901; rm -rf /tmp/x' and '$(id)')

title: sbp cass probe timeout is 30s but a cold probe takes 3m45s — the real cause of the rebuild ritual
description:
Measured on this box 2026-07-25 while implementing skillbox-ztaa (commit 7bcfeab in skillbox-config): the cass search probe takes 3m45s COLD and 8-11s WARM against the 2.3GB agent_search.db / 16GB tantivy index.

sbp_cass.py's probe uses timeout_probe=30. So a cold probe is killed at 30s, and because the search JSON and the trailing 'stat db_mtime' run in the SAME bash_remote call, both die together — producing exactly the signature the ztaa bead reported as evidence of a dead index:
  probe.search_total_matches = null
  db_mtime = null
...with the index perfectly healthy.

This means the recorded 'agent burns 9 minutes on a blocking rebuild' ritual was likely triggered by a TIMEOUT misread as a dead index, not by an actually-dead index. ztaa made the cron honest and self-healing and deliberately does not rebuild on a capped probe, but the false-alarm at the sbp front door remains until this is fixed.

Options, cheapest first:
1. Raise timeout_probe well above the cold-probe cost, or make it adaptive.
2. Split the search probe and the db_mtime stat into separate calls so a slow search cannot null out the mtime.
3. Make the probe cheap — a bounded single-term search with --fields minimal, or read a cached last-probe-ok marker. ztaa already writes /srv/skillbox/state/cass/last-probe-ok (format: '<ISO8601> matches=<n>'); _run_cheap_probes can read it in one line.

Also still open from ztaa: surface last-probe-ok in 'sbp cass status' output. sbp_cass.py was off-limits to that bead.
close_reason: Implemented in skillbox-config b2b8ec9: split stat from search, marker fast path, cap 30->300s, probe.state ok|zero|capped. 36 tests OK re-verified; live 'sbp cass status --json' re-measured independently at 0.458s returning status=ok with matches=229719 and non-null db_mtime, where the same command previously took 25.4s and returned null/null with an error. Corrected the bead's timings: warm 3.2s, cold 32.6s (not 3m45s/8-11s) - the causal claim (cold exceeds the 25s effective cap) held and was reproduced literally

comments.author: skillbox
comments.text:
2026-07-25 measurement correction for the record. This bead's description quoted 3m45s cold / 8-11s warm, inherited from skillbox-ztaa. Direct re-measurement during the fix gave: warm 3.2s; cold 32.6s (page cache for the 18.54GB db+index evicted per-file via unprivileged posix_fadvise(DONTNEED) — deliberately NOT drop_caches on a box with 41 live users, so this is a milder cold than ztaa's); 58.5s end-to-end through 'sbp cass status --live-probe' under load 9-14. The exact figures differ by eviction method, but the load-bearing claim was exact and was reproduced literally: cold cost exceeds the 25s effective cap, yielding null/null on a healthy index.

Additional finding that killed one proposed option: a bounded single-term search is NOT cheaper than '*' (33.8s vs 32.6s cold). Cold cost is index open and page-in, not query breadth. Only the marker read is genuinely cheap, which is why the fast path reads last-probe-ok rather than issuing a narrower query.
