title: Make sbp cass rebuild non-fatal on archive upload failure
description:
Friction: sbp cass rebuild gates the entire index rebuild on a prerequisite archive upload to R2 (sbp_cass.py lines 531-541). If the upload fails (network timeout, stale creds, SCP failure), rebuild returns early with exit 2 — the mirror-sync and reindex on lines 550-575 never execute. Agents get a false failure and the index stays stale.

Cass evidence: session d1664698 line 142-155 (prior rebuild), current session 2026-06-10 (archive_upload_error hit on this box).

Lube fix (smallest durable unblocker): Demote upload failure from fatal gate to warning. Record it in the payload as archive_upload_warning. Proceed with existing mirror data. Add --strict flag to preserve fatal behavior for CI.

No-ragrets contract:
- Outcome: sbp cass rebuild is self-healing — a flaky upload does not leave the index degraded.
- Evidence: two sessions where archive_upload_error blocked a rebuild that had viable local mirror data.
- Failure avoided: operator or agent runs sbp cass rebuild, gets exit 2, leaves index degraded, wastes a session re-diagnosing.
- Acceptance: (1) rebuild completes index even when upload fails, (2) payload contains archive_upload_warning, (3) --strict restores fatal, (4) existing tests pass.
close_reason: Demoted archive upload from fatal gate to warning; added --strict flag. Rebuild now continues with existing mirror data on upload failure. 4 tests verify non-fatal behavior, warning payload, and strict mode.

title: CASS immediate evidence fallback: recent logs instead of rebuild during active work
description:
Future behavior: when CASS is stale, degraded, or unavailable during an active agent task, agents should not rebuild the CASS index. They should use the recent-log/local transcript fallback path that skill-issue already documents for transcript evidence, then record that the evidence mode was degraded.

No-ragrets success contract:
- Outcome: skill-issue/CASS-facing guidance gives agents an exact fallback command/path for immediate evidence needs when CASS freshness is insufficient.
- Evidence: future agents encountering stale CASS use recent logs/local transcript scanning and report degraded evidence mode, rather than running sbp cass rebuild mid-task.
- Failure avoided: agents stall on index rebuilds, mutate local-machine search state, or skip evidence gathering entirely because CASS is stale.

Implementation considerations:
- Audit skill-issue evidence backend docs and sbp cass error/next_actions surfaces for stale/degraded CASS behavior.
- Prefer adding explicit next_actions such as skill-issue local scanner / recent transcript log path over adding any rebuild command.
- If the fallback belongs in skill-issue SKILL.md, use no-ragrets + skill-issue validation before editing.
- If the fallback belongs in sbp cass output, keep stdout/stderr and JSON contracts compact and testable.

Acceptance criteria:
1. Stale/degraded CASS guidance names a recent-log/local transcript fallback and does not recommend rebuild during active work.
2. The fallback path is tested or validated with a representative stale-CASS fixture or documented degraded-mode smoke.
3. skill-issue validation runs if SKILL.md changes.
4. Agent-facing output names the evidence mode so future users can tell CASS was bypassed.

Validation candidates: skill-issue quick_validate.py if edited; sbp cass status/search degraded-mode smoke if the CLI surface changes; focused tests for any changed runtime/sbp code.
close_reason: Documented degraded CASS evidence mode and local transcript fallback in bundled skill-issue guidance and sbp capabilities/help; validated with degraded sbp cass status smoke and focused tests.

title: Make cass search error on missing query argument
description:
Friction: cass search invoked with no query token in 96% of invocations (396 of 414 observed). Agents paste the bare command template from SKILL.md without filling in the query. cass silently returns empty or full corpus instead of erroring, so the agent doesn't realize the mistake.

Cass evidence: prior deep-dive session 9c51acce — command-shape histogram across all projects. 396/414 cass search calls had no positional arg.

Lube fix (smallest durable unblocker): Two changes: (1) cass search with no argv prints a one-line "missing QUERY positional — example: cass search 'foo bar'" and exits non-zero. (2) cass SKILL.md: replace bare cass search examples with cass search "<intent>" and add "the query is required" callout.

No-ragrets contract:
- Outcome: agents get immediate feedback when they omit the query, instead of silently getting useless results.
- Evidence: 96% misuse rate across 414 invocations — the current silent behavior trains agents to believe cass search is broken.
- Failure avoided: agent invokes cass search, gets empty results, concludes cass is broken, falls back to raw grep (observed in 72 sessions).
- Acceptance: (1) cass search with no args exits non-zero with usage hint, (2) SKILL.md examples include query placeholder, (3) cass search "real query" still works.
notes: BLOCKER: requires changes to cass binary. cass search must error when invoked without a query argument instead of silently returning empty.

title: cass indexes only 2419 of 6542 projected claude files — 3381 agent-* sidechains never enter the index
description:
Measured 2026-07-25 while implementing skillbox-vev1 (skillbox-config 3770799): of 6542 projected claude files, cass indexes only 2419. Of the 4331 'agent-*' sidechain files, 3381 never enter the index at all.

This — not the flat projection bucket — is one of the two real drivers of low per-repo mining yield. vev1 proved the projection directory name is irrelevant to workspace attribution (cass derives workspace only from the JSONL cwd field), so fixing layout did not and could not raise these counts.

Investigate why the sidechains are skipped: file shape, size threshold, a session-type filter, or an indexer error being swallowed. Compare an indexed file against a skipped sidechain of the same generation.

Evidence to reproduce: count files under /srv/skillbox/state/cass/source-projection/current/.claude/projects/ vs conversations in agent_search.db.
close_reason: Implemented in skillbox-config b44fc91: bounded mtime re-arm batch with ledger + mtime restore. 57 tests OK re-verified. Root cause is NOT file shape: a capped --force-rebuild leaves a contiguous tail unindexed, and cass only discovers files with mtime > meta.last_scan_ts, so the follow-up incremental stamps them invisible forever. Counts confirmed exactly (6542/2419 in restored/, 3381 of 4331 agent-* skipped). DEPLOYMENT CAUTION recorded in comments: disk headroom is insufficient to drain the full backlog

comments.author: skillbox
comments.text:
2026-07-25 DEPLOYMENT CAUTION — disk, measured not estimated.

The fix is live immediately on commit because ~/.local/bin/cass-mirror-sync.sh is a SYMLINK to the repo file. The 21:30 tick already picked it up and started an index run (pid 2249156, 'cass index --json --no-progress-events --data-dir /srv/skillbox/state/cass/current').

Capacity arithmetic against the live index:
- index 15.07 GB for 8976 conversations = ~1.8 MB per conversation
- backlog is 4123 files; observed ratio is ~2 conversations per file, so ~8200 more conversations
- projected growth ~13-14 GB
- free space on / is 8.1 GB, and the filesystem is already at 95%

Draining the full backlog at 250/tick (~17 ticks, ~8.5h) would very likely fill the root filesystem on a box with 41 logged-in users. Filling / is far worse than the under-indexing it fixes.

Recommended sequencing:
1. Add CASS_MIRROR_BACKFILL=0 to the cron line to hold further batches (the backlog is still counted and reported in the JSON either way, so visibility is retained).
2. Recover space first. 514 MB of nx5m sandboxes remain at /srv/skillbox/state/cass-sandbox{,2,3,4}-nx5m; dcg correctly refuses rm -rf on those paths (core.filesystem:rm-rf-root-home), so the operator must remove them manually.
3. Re-enable, ideally with a smaller batch and a disk-headroom precondition. A guard that refuses to backfill below N GB free would make this safe to leave on permanently — worth its own bead.

title: Add Conference1 tailnet Serve and heavy-build visibility to SBP
description:
Context:
Conference1 is now the preferred heavy local machine for Swimmers-style Rust builds/tests and has working Tailscale Serve mappings for tailnet-only dev surfaces. Current host facts from the setup run:
- Tailscale MagicDNS: conference1.tailexample.ts.net
- Tailscale IP: 100.100.1.1
- SSH automation path: worker@100.100.1.1, with WSL Ubuntu for build workloads
- Windows helper for true Tailscale Serve: C:\Users\worker\bin\tailnet-serve.ps1 list|expose|remove
- Active Serve mappings use MagicDNS host URLs and forward to 127.0.0.1 backends on ports 3000, 3001, 3170, 3210, and 8050
- Raw Tailscale-IP portproxy exists as fallback, but the durable/clean path should be Tailscale Serve and tailnet-only semantics

Problem:
This knowledge currently lives in operator chat and machine-local helpers. Skillbox/SBP should expose it as first-class environment metadata and commands so future agents do not rediscover the same host/port/Tailscale constraints or keep using the wrong machine for heavy Swimmers validation.

Requested work:
1. Add Conference1 to the appropriate Skillbox/SBP environment metadata so agents can discover it as a heavy-build/dev-surface target.
2. Add or extend an SBP/Skillbox command surface that can list the known Conference1 tailnet URLs and, where appropriate, call the Windows tailnet-serve helper over SSH to list/expose/remove ports.
3. Keep app startup in repo-local scripts or app package scripts; keep Tailscale Serve management in host/SBP infrastructure, not random npm scripts.
4. Capture the Swimmers remote Rust validation lane: SWIMMERS_REMOTE_RUST_HOST=conference1-ssh or worker@100.100.1.1 plus WSL Ubuntu and persistent Cargo cache /var/tmp/swimmers-remote-rust-cache.
5. Document the security rule clearly: use Tailscale Serve/MagicDNS for tailnet access, do not require 0.0.0.0 public binds, and do not use Funnel unless explicitly requested.

Acceptance criteria:
- From the d/Skillbox environment, an agent can run one documented command to see Conference1 endpoints, helper commands, and current Serve status.
- The command output distinguishes MagicDNS Serve URLs from raw-IP portproxy fallback URLs.
- The implementation has at least one focused test or fixture proving Conference1 metadata renders without leaking secrets.
- README/agent docs mention the operator workflow briefly enough that future agents can route Swimmers heavy validation to Conference1 without chat archaeology.
- Proof includes a tailnet-only posture check or documented manual check path.
notes: ROUTING: requires Conference1 machine access and private overlay configuration. Operator-specific infrastructure bead — needs private skillbox-config context.

'sbp conference1 status' shows endpoints/helper/serve state live from this environment; output distinguishes MagicDNS Serve URLs (primary) from raw-IP portproxy fallback; metadata in existing scripts/clipboard/hosts.json registry incl. Swimmers remote Rust lane (SWIMMERS_REMOTE_RUST_HOST=conference1-ssh, WSL Ubuntu, /var/tmp/swimmers-remote-rust-cache); expose/remove dry-run by default + --yes gate, Funnel refused; secret-shape leak guard tested; docs/conference1.md documents workflow + tailnet-only posture check; AGENTS.md pointer added. comments.text:
2026-07-25 from skillbox-dcg-hook-convergence-v2mu (commit 8c8f278): docker-compose.yml now mounts ${SKILLBOX_STATE_ROOT}/home/.config/dcg into all 3 services, carrying the user policy render, the reconcile ledger, and rollback backups. Without it a container recreate loses the ledger that binds Codex's persisted hook-trust hash to the exact hooks.json bytes, so a converged home silently looks fresh and untrusted.

The mount is compose-only, matching the existing pattern for .config/claude-code, .config/git, .config/gh and .grok, which are likewise absent from workspace/persistence.yaml. If this bead wants it in expected_mounts, add the binding here — it was outside v2mu's write set.

comments.author: skillbox
comments.text:
2026-07-25 URGENT, verified twice: a plain non-isolated 'manage sync' currently REOPENS FAIL-OPEN on this box.

runtime_ops._dcg_config_content emits only a header, [packs] enabled, and optionally an [allowlist] rules table. It emits NO [general] table and NO fail_closed key — confirmed by reading the function source directly, independent of the agent that reported it. The live .dcg.toml (sha256 51fee6be…, committed policy render) DOES carry '[general] fail_closed = true'. So any ordinary sync overwrites it with a config that drops fail_closed, and unparseable hook input stops being denied.

skillbox-sync-dcg-config-state-root-934w (commit 68680fb) closed only the ISOLATED-run vector: a sync under a foreign SKILLBOX_STATE_ROOT now refuses to write. A normal sync in this repo still clobbers.

Concrete work for this bead, in order:
1. Replace the _dcg_config_content call inside sync_dcg_config with dcg_policy.render(), feeding _dcg_packs_and_allowlist's client-overlay packs/allowlist in as the OVERLAY so APPROVED_PACKS and the wildcard-allowlist validation actually apply. The legacy '[allowlist] rules = [...]' table should die with it — dcg 0.6.7's AllowlistConfig has no such key, so those rules have always been a silent no-op (see skillbox-dcg-policy-contract-po63, commit f72e909).
2. Fix _dcg_config_current: it compares against LEGACY text, so against a policy-rendered file it reports a diff on every sync and rewrites unconditionally instead of returning 'exists:'. That is the mechanism that makes the clobber happen every time.
3. Decide whether client dcg.packs entries outside APPROVED_PACKS become a hard ValidationError during sync, or a skipped-with-reason action.

68680fb's gate is a pure pre-check that returns before packs or content are computed, so the renderer swap is a drop-in. Keep the gate.

Until this lands, treat 'manage sync' as a guard-disarming operation on this repo.

title: Deep research (GTM): Which channels + content formats drive OSS dev-tool CLI adoption for single-operator infra projects?
description:
**Why this matters for skillbox (marketing/GTM):** skillbox is an OSS CLI/Docker project targeting independent developers and consultants who want a private Tailnet-first agent workstation. Unlike SaaS dev tools, its acquisition path is entirely community-driven — GitHub discovery, developer word-of-mouth, Show HN, and ecosystem cross-links. Understanding which specific distribution moves (awesome-lists, comparisons, HN posts, X threads, YouTube walkthroughs) actually drive sustained GitHub star growth and downstream forks/installs for comparable single-operator infra OSS projects would define whether to invest in content, community presence, or focused comparison pages.

**Round-1 deep-research already covers:** Tailscale-first private agent infra adoption vs managed runtimes (product/market landscape).

---

## Deep research prompt (marketing / GTM / SEO / content)

**Role + mission:** You are an OSS developer-tool growth researcher. Your sole task is to identify which specific distribution channels, content formats, and community engagement tactics drive sustained GitHub star growth and downstream adoption for single-operator infrastructure CLI tools (not SaaS, not team dev-platforms) in 2026. You do NOT analyze product-market fit, compare architectures, or produce generic marketing advice.

**Context:**

skillbox is an open-source CLI + Docker-based personal agent workstation for independent developers running coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor) on a private Tailscale-connected machine. It is a single-operator tool — not a team platform, not a SaaS. Its closest comparators are personal infra OSS projects like Devbox, DevPod, and small CLI tooling repos, not enterprise dev platforms like Coder or Gitpod.

The decision this output informs: Rob needs to choose 2–3 concrete distribution moves to execute in the next 30–60 days. Should he write a "my private agent workstation setup" blog post or X thread? Submit to specific awesome-lists? Post a Show HN? Record a short walkthrough video? Get listed in comparison pages? The answer depends on what has actually worked for comparable projects at similar star counts (50–500 range), not on generic "OSS growth playbooks."

The ICP is: solo developers and indie consultants who run AI coding agents, want durable reproducible dev environments, already use Tailscale or SSH-first workflows, and are dissatisfied with ephemeral agent contexts. They discover new tools via GitHub trending, HN, X threads from developers they follow, and curated awesome-lists.

Good output looks like: "Projects like [X] went from 150 to 800 stars in 90 days primarily via a Show HN post that framed the problem as 'my coding agents forget everything' — here are the specific elements that worked, and here are the awesome-lists/community channels that amplified it."

**Research questions:**

1. **GitHub star-velocity case studies**: Find 5–8 OSS projects in the single-operator dev-infra / personal agent workspace / CLI tooling space (not SaaS, not team tools) that grew from ~50 to 500+ GitHub stars in 2024–2026. For each: repo name | peak growth period | primary acquisition channel | content format that triggered the spike | approximate stars/week during launch. Use Star History, HN Algolia search, and public GitHub data.

2. **Show HN effectiveness for this category**: Search HN Algolia (hn.algolia.com) for Show HN posts about personal dev infra, agent workstations, local AI tooling, CLI dev environments from 2024–2026. What point counts, comment volumes, and stated traffic spikes did the best-performing posts achieve? What made the top 5 posts work (framing, demo format, README quality, timing)?

3. **Awesome-list and curator leverage**: Which awesome-lists and GitHub curator lists (e.g., awesome-selfhosted, awesome-devenv, awesome-claude, awesome-ai-tools) include comparable tools? What traffic/star impact do inclusions typically generate? Which lists are most relevant for skillbox's niche and have open submission processes?

4. **X / Twitter dev-influencer channel**: Which X accounts with 5k–100k developer followers regularly post about personal AI tooling, agent workflows, Tailscale setups, or CLI dev environments? What content formats (threads, short demos, before/after comparisons) get the most engagement in this niche? Find 3–5 real examples with engagement data.

5. **Comparison page / alternative-to SEO**: Do comparison pages like AlternativeTo, Slant, ProductHunt, or developer-written "X vs Y" blog posts drive meaningful traffic for single-operator infra tools? What's the evidence from comparable projects (DevPod, Devbox, Daytona at early stage)? Is "skillbox vs Coder/Gitpod/Devbox" content a realistic SEO play given domain authority constraints?

6. **Founder-led / build-in-public mechanics**: For OSS projects at this stage (sub-500 stars, solo founder), what does effective "build in public" look like in 2026 — weekly changelogs on X, GitHub Discussion updates, Discord community building, or something else? Find 3–5 real examples from 2024–2026 with measurable outcomes.

7. **GEO / AI-search citation opportunity**: What queries do developers use in ChatGPT, Perplexity, or Google when looking for "private coding agent workstation", "self-hosted dev environment for AI agents", "Claude Code home directory setup", "Tailscale dev box"? Which sources currently appear in AI overviews for these? What content format (README, blog post, docs page, comparison page) consistently earns LLM citations for CLI dev tools?

**Output format:**

### Star-Velocity Case Studies
One block per project: Project | Stars then → now | Growth period | Primary channel | Content trigger | Stars/week peak | Source.

### Show HN Effectiveness
Table: Post title | Points | Comments | Stated traffic/star impact | Key success factors. Plus 2–3 paragraph synthesis.

### Awesome-List / Curator Map
Table: List name | Estimated monthly views | Stars impact per inclusion (evidence or inferred) | Relevance to skillbox | Open submissions?.

### X Influencer Map
Table: Account | Followers | Niche | Best-performing content format | Engagement benchmarks.

### Comparison Page / SEO Viability
2–3 paragraphs on whether this is worth pursuing at skillbox's current stage, with evidence.

### Build-in-Public Playbook
Ranked list of 3–5 tactics with evidence sources and confidence flags.

### GEO / AI-Search Opportunity
5–8 specific query strings with: current top cited source | content gap | recommended content format.

### Prioritized 30–60 Day Distribution Plan
Top 3 moves ranked by (reach × conversion) / effort, each with a one-sentence rationale and confidence flag.

**Hard constraints:**
- No generic OSS growth listicles. Ban Orbit, Common Room, DEV.to generic guides, and generic "how to market your OSS project" posts as sources.
- All star counts, HN points, and engagement numbers must be cited or marked "inferred/not verified."
- Focus exclusively on single-operator infra tools, not team SaaS, not enterprise dev platforms.
- Do not cover product architecture, build-vs-buy, or private agent infra adoption (Round 1 territory).
- Use primary sources: GitHub, HN Algolia, Reddit, Star History, X search.
- Flag all confidence levels explicitly.

**Completion criteria:**
1. Star-velocity case studies cover at least 5 real projects with cited data.
2. Show HN section covers at least 5 real posts with point/comment data.
3. Awesome-list map has at least 5 lists with relevance assessment.
4. GEO section has at least 5 query strings with source analysis.
5. Prioritized plan gives exactly 3 moves with confidence flags.
close_reason: Completed sourced report at docs/research/2026-06-01-oss-cli-distribution-research.md; evidence gaps: GitHub traffic/referrals, awesome-list referral impact, primary X engagement/follower metrics, and AI-search citation behavior were not publicly verifiable.

title: Deep research: What is the real adoption curve for Tailscale-first private agent infrastructure vs managed cloud agent runtimes?
description:
**Why this matters for skillbox:** skillbox's entire architectural bet — Tailscale as the access primitive, one durable private machine, operator-owned infrastructure — only wins if there is a durable cohort of developers who (a) are building seriously with AI coding agents, (b) prefer SSH + private VPS over browser IDEs and managed sandboxes, and (c) will not be swept into a Coder/Daytona/E2B managed offering as those mature. If Tailscale adoption among developer-infra builders is flat or regressing (or if Cloudflare Tunnel is eating the "private developer infra" niche), skillbox's distribution assumptions break. This research would directly shape the Phase 1–3 roadmap priority and whether to bet more on the Tailscale-native identity/access model or treat it as an optional transport.

---

## Deep research prompt

You are a developer-infrastructure analyst. Your sole task is to assess the adoption trajectory of Tailscale (and comparable private-network tools) among AI-agent developers and coding-assistant users, and to compare this against the managed-cloud-runtime trajectory (E2B, Daytona, GitHub Codespaces agent mode, Cursor hosted). You do NOT evaluate financial performance, investment prospects, or general enterprise IT Tailscale deployments outside the developer-tool context.

### Context

A CLI-first project called skillbox is built around the thesis that serious independent AI-coding-agent operators want a durable, single-tenant, Tailscale-connected private machine rather than ephemeral managed sandboxes or browser IDEs. The Tailscale access layer is not cosmetic — it drives how skill distribution, shared-box collaborator access (shared-jam), and remote runtime invocations work.

The research exists because this design has a key external dependency: the developer community using Tailscale as infrastructure for their own tooling must be large enough and growing fast enough that tooling built for it has a real addressable base. If the community is tiny or stagnating while managed offerings grow, the distribution path changes. If Tailscale is winning hard (developer blog posts, Homebrew installs, Discord communities, job postings requiring Tailscale), the bet is reinforced.

The audience for this research is the project maintainer deciding whether to deepen Tailscale-native features (richer node tagging, exit-node routing, ACL-based skill access), add a Cloudflare/WireGuard compatibility layer, or accept Tailscale as a project-scope constraint and focus only on users who have already adopted it.

Good research here means: concrete adoption evidence (install counts, developer blog references, open-source project dependencies, community size signals) for Tailscale in the developer-infra segment specifically, alongside competing private-network tools and the managed-cloud alternatives, so the project can calibrate how big its natural user base is.

### Research Questions

1. What is the current evidence for Tailscale adoption specifically among developer-infra and AI-coding-agent users? (Look for: Tailscale blog references to developer workflows, open-source projects on GitHub that list Tailscale as a dependency or in their README/docs, community Discord/Reddit presence, developer blog posts with significant engagement.)
2. What competing private-networking approaches (WireGuard raw, Cloudflare Tunnel, ZeroTier, Netbird, Headscale self-hosted) are developers in the AI-agent/coding-tool space actually using, and what are their stated reasons for choosing one over another?
3. What is the current feature gap and pricing comparison between Tailscale free/personal tier and the next tier up? Has this changed in 2024–2026 in ways that would push solo developers away or toward it?
4. What is the published adoption data or analyst estimates for E2B, Daytona, GitHub Codespaces (for agent use), and Cursor hosted environments among independent developers versus enterprise teams? Which cohort is growing faster?
5. Are there public developer surveys (Stack Overflow Developer Survey, JetBrains State of Developer Ecosystem, GitHub Octoverse, or similar) that capture data on remote development environment preferences or AI-coding-agent infrastructure preferences?
6. What do high-signal developer community threads (Hacker News "Ask HN", lobste.rs, r/selfhosted, r/devops) say about the tradeoff between "managed ephemeral" vs "private durable" infrastructure for AI coding agents?

### Output Format

**Executive Summary** (3–5 bullets on the most decision-relevant findings about Tailscale adoption and the managed-vs-private tradeoff)

**Tailscale Adoption Evidence**
- Quantitative signals: install estimates, GitHub dependency count, community size
- Qualitative signals: developer blog post themes, forum sentiment
- Trend direction (growing / flat / unknown) with confidence rating

**Competing Private-Network Tools** (one entry each for WireGuard DIY, Cloudflare Tunnel, Netbird, ZeroTier, Headscale)
- What it is and who uses it
- Evidence of developer-infra adoption
- Key reasons developers cite for choosing it over Tailscale
- Confidence: [high / medium / low]

**Managed Agent Runtime Adoption**
- E2B: evidence of adoption level, target user segment, growth signals
- Daytona: same
- GitHub Codespaces agent mode: same
- Cursor hosted / other: same
- Cross-entity synthesis: is the managed tier winning among solo devs, enterprise, or both?

**Survey and Report Data**
- Any developer surveys that address remote dev environment preferences (2024–2026)
- What they say about private-box vs managed preferences

**Developer Community Sentiment**
- 3–5 representative thread summaries (HN, Reddit, lobste.rs) on the managed-vs-private question, with URLs and engagement counts

**Uncertainty Log**
- All claims marked "not found" or "inferred" with confidence notes

### Hard Constraints

- Authoritative sources only: Tailscale official blog, GitHub repositories, credible developer press (The New Stack, InfoQ, Ars Technica, Hacker News with high engagement), official survey reports (Stack Overflow, JetBrains, GitHub Octoverse). Do NOT cite Wikipedia, Crunchbase, G2, or tool-comparison listicle sites as primary evidence.
- Every quantitative claim (install count, GitHub star count, pricing tier detail) must be cited or marked "not found / inferred."
- Do not fabricate blog post titles, forum thread URLs, or survey statistics.
- Scope: developer-infra and AI-agent tooling only. General enterprise Tailscale deployments, gaming VPNs, and home-network uses are out of scope unless they cross into the developer-tool community.
- Flag all uncertain claims with "confidence: low, needs human review."
- No marketing prose; produce an analyst's evidence brief.

### Completion Criteria

Report is complete when:
1. All six research questions have answers or explicit "not found" notes.
2. Tailscale adoption evidence section has at least three quantitative or semi-quantitative signals.
3. At least four competing private-network tools have per-tool entries.
4. At least three managed agent runtimes have adoption evidence with trend direction.
5. All sources are cited inline or in a reference list.
close_reason: Completed dated developer-infra research artifact with Tailscale adoption evidence, private-network competitors, managed agent runtime comparison, survey data, community sentiment, uncertainty log, and validation checks.

title: Productize devl clipboard, tmux, mosh, SSH, and image transfer bootstrap for new Skillbox hosts
description:
Context:
A live operator fix in /Users/b/.local/share/devl proved the desired end state for copy/paste across the operator Mac, local tmux, d0/d1/d2/d3 launcher paths, mosh, SSH, remote tmux, Conference1 WSL, Sweet Potato, Jeremy, and the default d3 portfolio devbox. That fix currently lives outside the Skillbox repo as local devl scripts and remote home-directory installs. It should become a first-class Skillbox bootstrap capability so every new or rebuilt host gets the same copy/paste behavior without chat archaeology.

What the live proof established:
- Ghostty accepts OSC52 clipboard writes when launched as a real terminal with clipboard-write=allow.
- Local tmux can copy to the Mac clipboard when the managed tmux fragment uses the helper.
- Direct SSH and direct mosh to portfolio-devbox.example can copy to the Mac clipboard.
- Remote tmux over mosh initially failed even though `tmux load-buffer -w` returned success; the durable fix was for `clipcopy` to populate the tmux buffer and write OSC52 directly to attached tmux client TTYs discovered via `tmux list-clients -F '#{client_name}'`.
- `conference1-ssh` via Windows -> WSL broke OSC52; direct `conference1-wsl` works over SSH and mosh. d0/d2/d3 should prefer the direct WSL target and only fall back to the Windows wrapper when the WSL target is unavailable.
- Remotes need xterm-ghostty terminfo installed or Ghostty-launched SSH sessions can make tmux fail with `missing or unsuitable terminal: xterm-ghostty`.
- The image stretch goal is feasible as a local macOS helper that reads PNG/TIFF from NSPasteboard, uploads it to a target's ~/clipboard-images directory, verifies the remote file, and puts the remote path back on the local clipboard.

Goal:
Move this from ad hoc local state into Skillbox as a reusable, testable, documented bootstrap surface for current d3 targets and future boxes. The final result should let an agent or operator run one documented command during host adoption and get text clipboard and image-transfer support across local tmux, SSH, mosh, remote tmux, and supported WSL targets.

Completion contract:
This epic is complete only when the child beads land the source bundle, bootstrap/install integration, route metadata, proof harnesses, image helper, docs, current-host rollout, and closeout verification. Do not close this epic just because a local devl copy exists; Skillbox must own the durable source of truth and new-host initiation path.

title: Define the Skillbox clipboard bootstrap contract and supported host matrix
description:
Purpose:
Before moving scripts, write the explicit contract Skillbox is going to own. The current implementation was proven live, but the repo needs a durable design target so future agents do not cargo-cult shell snippets.

Scope:
Create a concise design note or architecture section for Skillbox clipboard bootstrap. It should define supported surfaces and the behavior expected on each:
- operator macOS + Ghostty + local tmux
- portfolio-devbox.example default d3 target over SSH and mosh
- remote tmux inside portfolio-devbox.example sessions such as d2/devbox-N
- Sweet Potato (`aiops@sweet-potato.example`) over SSH
- Jeremy (`skillbox@jeremy-vps.example`) over SSH
- Conference1 WSL via direct `conference1-wsl` over SSH/mosh
- last-resort `conference1-ssh` Windows wrapper, explicitly documented as an OSC52-hostile fallback, not the preferred copy/paste path

The note must record the important implementation findings:
1. OSC52 is the portable text clipboard mechanism.
2. tmux `set-clipboard on` and `terminal-features ... clipboard` are necessary but not sufficient for remote tmux over mosh.
3. `tmux load-buffer -w` can return success while failing to update the outer clipboard on the mosh path; Skillbox must preserve the direct attached-client TTY write in `clipcopy`.
4. `xterm-ghostty` terminfo must exist in user terminfo on remotes that may receive Ghostty-launched SSH sessions.
5. Image transfer is file upload plus remote-path paste, not true binary paste into a terminal. That limitation is acceptable and should be named honestly.

Acceptance criteria:
- The design is self-contained and links to the future source location for helper scripts.
- The host matrix distinguishes required, best-effort, and known-bad/fallback paths.
- The design names security boundaries: no secrets, no public exposure, no Tailscale Funnel, no broad 0.0.0.0 service binding, and no accidental writes outside user homes except approved bootstrap-managed locations.
- The design includes an adoption checklist for new hosts: install helper bundle, source tmux fragment, install terminfo, verify real-terminal copy, verify image upload.

Validation:
- Reviewer can read only this bead plus the design note and understand why the final implementation differs from a trivial `set -g set-clipboard on` change.

title: Add closeout gates and regression checks for clipboard bootstrap
description:
Purpose:
Prevent this from regressing after it is moved into Skillbox. The live session found multiple ways a superficially green setup can still fail: tmux options present but no OS clipboard update; direct SSH works but remote tmux fails; Conference Windows wrapper reachable but OSC52-hostile; terminfo missing only when launched from Ghostty.

Required gates:
- Static checks: shell syntax, shellcheck where available, git diff --check.
- Unit/fixture checks: installer idempotency, route selection, target mapping, tilde normalization, tmux fragment content, direct client-TTY behavior in clipcopy.
- Host checks: terminfo presence, helper executability, tmux option state.
- Real-terminal checks: local tmux, SSH, mosh, remote tmux, nested local+remote tmux, Conference direct WSL path.
- Image checks: synthetic PNG upload and remote file verification.

Acceptance criteria:
- The closeout checklist is encoded in docs, tests, or a script so future agents can run it without reconstructing commands from memory.
- The gate distinguishes mocked/unit proof from live terminal proof.
- The gate restores local clipboard content and cleans temporary tmux sockets/sessions.
- The gate names any host skipped and why.
- The final closeout records exact command output evidence and any residual limitations.

Validation:
- Run the full closeout command suite at least once after implementation.
- `br dep cycles --json` returns no cycles.
- `br sync --flush-only` and `br sync --status` show the tracker is exported.

Checklist encoded in scripts/clipboard-closeout.sh + docs; gate distinguishes unit vs live proof, restores local clipboard, cleans tmux sockets/sessions, names skipped hosts with reasons, emits durable JSON artifacts with raw logs. title: Completion debt: make clipboard closeout prove live terminal paths instead of passing skipped proof
description:
Context:

Scope:
Upgrade the closeout/proof harness so it can distinguish source-level unit confidence from rollout-level operator proof.

Required behavior:

- A documented command exists for CI/source smoke and a separate documented command exists for operator/live rollout proof.

description:
Context:
The current implementation provides a standalone CLI and docs, but the audit did not find integration into box.py, env-manager lifecycle, install.sh, or another automatic new-host adoption hook. This may be acceptable if clipboard bootstrap is intentionally operator-run, but the Beads should make that product decision explicit.

- Wire clipboard bootstrap into the appropriate new-host lifecycle surface, such as scripts/box.py enroll/post-enroll, install.sh, env-manager runtime commands, or another existing Skillbox adoption workflow.
- Or explicitly document that clipboard bootstrap remains a manual operator/agent command, with rationale, exact command, and proof that agents bootstrapping a new server will see the instruction early enough.

Acceptance verified: single discoverable adoption path in docs/operations.md cross-linked from AGENTS.md and docs/clipboard-bootstrap.md; docs no longer imply --profile d3 writes remotely without --apply-remote (fixed wording, dry-run-first pattern); fresh-checkout validation commands documented and executed — scripts/clipboard-bootstrap --profile d3 prints plan exit 0 with no remote writes; tests.test_clipboard_bootstrap OK. title: Move the managed clipboard helper bundle into Skillbox source control
description:
Purpose:
Make Skillbox, not ~/.local/share/devl, the source of truth for the clipboard integration. The local devl version currently has these pieces:
- clipboard/clipcopy
- clipboard/clippaste
- clipboard/pbcopy shim for Linux remotes
- clipboard/clipimg-put
- clipboard/tmux.conf
- devl-clipboard-install

Requested implementation:
Create an appropriate Skillbox-owned location for the bundle, for example `scripts/clipboard/`, `home/.local/share/skillbox/clipboard/`, or another path that matches existing repo conventions. Preserve the behavior proven live:
- `clipcopy` reads stdin into a temp file.
- On local macOS without SSH, it uses `/usr/bin/pbcopy`.
- Inside tmux, it loads the tmux buffer and then writes OSC52 to attached client TTYs from `tmux list-clients -F '#{client_name}'`, falling back to `tmux load-buffer -w` only if no client TTY write succeeds.
- Outside tmux on remote SSH/mosh, it emits OSC52 to `/dev/tty`.
- `clippaste` uses local `/usr/bin/pbpaste` when safe and otherwise saves the current tmux buffer; it must not pretend remote terminals can read the Mac clipboard without a paste action.
- Linux `pbcopy` shim delegates to `clipcopy` so tools expecting pbcopy can still work.
- tmux fragment sets `set-clipboard on`, stable `terminal-features` with clipboard/RGB entries for xterm, Ghostty, tmux, and screen terms, and copy-mode bindings to the absolute installed helper path.
- installer installs helper scripts, tmux fragment, and local macOS image helper with idempotent sourcing in ~/.tmux.conf.

Acceptance criteria:
- The helper source is tracked in the Skillbox repo and no longer needs to be copied from a local devl-only directory for future host setup.
- Scripts are shellcheck-clean or have documented shellcheck limitations.
- Unit-style tests or golden checks verify that generated install paths and tmux fragment content include the client-TTY behavior and absolute helper binding.
- The installer is idempotent: repeated runs do not duplicate tmux source lines or append duplicate terminal-features entries.
- The code preserves ASCII-only scripts unless a specific terminal sequence requires escapes.

Validation:
- `bash -n` on all shell helpers.
- Focused unit test for installer/render behavior if implemented in Python or shell fixture tests if implemented as shell scripts.
- `git diff --check`.
close_reason: Shipped in Skillbox clipboard bootstrap epic (scripts/clipboard/, closeout, docs, tests)

title: Install and verify tmux clipboard profile plus xterm-ghostty terminfo on target hosts
description:
Purpose:
Capture the non-obvious host setup that made the live fix reliable. The main trap was not missing `set-clipboard`; it was terminfo plus tmux client behavior.

Scope:
Implement a Skillbox bootstrap step or reusable command that installs the managed tmux clipboard fragment and ensures `xterm-ghostty` terminfo exists for each managed host/user home that agents enter through d3-style launchers. The command must support at least:
- skillbox@portfolio-devbox.example
- aiops@sweet-potato.example
- skillbox@jeremy-vps.example
- worker@conference1-wsl

Required details:
- Install terminfo using `infocmp -x xterm-ghostty | tic -x -` or an equivalent tracked terminfo source.
- Verify with `infocmp -x xterm-ghostty >/dev/null` on the remote.
- Source the tmux fragment from ~/.tmux.conf without overwriting host-specific tmux settings.
- Start or address a tmux server only as needed for verification; do not kill live operator sessions.
- Preserve existing local tmux settings such as mouse, history-limit, NTM dashboard bindings, and host-specific environment tweaks.

Acceptance criteria:
- A new host can run one Skillbox command to install terminfo + tmux fragment for the current user.
- The command emits structured evidence showing helper paths, tmux `copy-command`, `set-clipboard`, and terminal feature entries.
- The command handles a host with no existing tmux server by using `tmux start-server \; ...` rather than failing on `no server running`.
- The command reports but does not destructively repair unrelated Beads/doctor warnings or remote tmux sessions.

Validation:
- On each supported target, proof includes `copy-command /home/<user>/.local/bin/clipcopy` (or equivalent), clipboard terminal features, and successful `infocmp -x xterm-ghostty`.
- Tests cover idempotent tmux source-line insertion and terminfo command rendering.

title: Encode the d3 Conference routing rule: prefer conference1-wsl directly, not the Windows WSL wrapper
description:
Purpose:
The live proof showed that Conference1 has two materially different automation routes:
- `conference1-wsl` direct WSL SSH target: OSC52 works over SSH and mosh, including remote tmux.
- `conference1-ssh` Windows SSH wrapper that invokes `wsl.exe`: useful as a recovery fallback, but OSC52 did not reach the Mac clipboard even outside tmux.

The d0/d2/d3 local scripts were patched in devl to prefer `conference1-wsl` directly, choose mosh there when `mosh-server` exists, otherwise use plain SSH, and fall back to `conference1-ssh`/WSL wrapper only when the direct WSL target is unreachable. Skillbox should own this routing knowledge so future launcher regeneration, docs, or host metadata do not regress to the broken wrapper path.

Requested work:
- Find the right Skillbox repo surface for d environment metadata or launcher generation. If local devl scripts are intentionally out of scope for Skillbox, encode the policy in docs plus an exportable metadata file that devl can consume later.
- Represent both Conference targets and their semantics: direct WSL target is preferred for terminal features and clipboard; Windows wrapper is fallback/recovery.
- Include a probe contract: `ssh conference1-wsl true`; then `ssh conference1-wsl 'command -v mosh-server'`; choose mosh/ssh accordingly.
- Do not assume mosh is always available; plain SSH to direct WSL is still clipboard-capable.

Acceptance criteria:
- Future agents can inspect Skillbox metadata/docs and know not to use `conference1-ssh` for clipboard-sensitive work unless direct WSL is down.
- Any generated d launcher or documented snippet reflects the direct-WSL-first order.
- The old wrapper path remains documented for auth/recovery cases but is explicitly labeled OSC52-hostile or clipboard fallback-only.
- Tests or fixtures assert the route-selection order for Conference1.

Validation:
- A route-selection unit test or documented command output proves direct `conference1-wsl` wins when reachable.
- Real proof command for Conference direct WSL copy is documented: Ghostty -> mosh/SSH -> conference1-wsl -> remote tmux -> clipcopy updates Mac clipboard.

title: Wire clipboard bootstrap into Skillbox new-host and adoption workflows
description:
Purpose:
A helper bundle in the repo is not enough; it must run naturally when a new Skillbox-style host becomes available. This bead turns the source bundle and host contract into a new-host initiation workflow.

title: Add real-terminal clipboard proof harnesses for local tmux, SSH, mosh, remote tmux, and nested tmux
description:
Purpose:
Codex's captured PTY did not pass OSC52 to the Mac clipboard, so ordinary command output is not enough to prove this feature. The live fix used disposable real Ghostty windows launched with `open -na Ghostty.app --args --clipboard-write=allow --confirm-close-surface=false -e <script>` and then polled `/usr/bin/pbpaste`. Skillbox needs a repeatable proof harness or documented manual equivalent.

Required proof cases:
1. Ghostty accepts a direct OSC52 write.
2. Ghostty -> local tmux -> clipcopy updates Mac clipboard.
3. Ghostty -> SSH -> remote clipcopy updates Mac clipboard.
4. Ghostty -> mosh -> remote clipcopy updates Mac clipboard.
5. Ghostty -> mosh -> remote tmux -> clipcopy updates Mac clipboard.
6. Ghostty -> local tmux -> mosh -> remote tmux -> clipcopy updates Mac clipboard.
7. Sweet and Jeremy remote tmux over SSH update Mac clipboard.
8. Conference direct `conference1-wsl` over SSH and mosh updates Mac clipboard, including remote tmux.

The harness must restore the previous local clipboard content after each test or at exit. It should use unique payloads and fail if the clipboard contains a stale value. It must clean up temporary tmux sockets and remote proof sessions. It must not kill unrelated tmux sessions.

Acceptance criteria:
- A single documented proof command can run the local plus selected remote cases.
- The harness can skip unavailable hosts with explicit SKIP output when configured to do so, but the release/adoption proof for a host must require PASS for that host.
- The harness records enough output to debug routing failures, terminfo failures, and tmux client failures.
- The exact bug found live is covered: `tmux load-buffer -w` success without clipboard update would fail the harness.

Validation:
- Run the harness locally against at least the default devbox before closing.
- Add unit tests for payload generation, clipboard restore trap command construction, and remote command quoting if the harness is scripted.
close_reason: Shipped in Skillbox clipboard bootstrap epic (scripts/clipboard/, closeout, docs, tests)

title: Productize clipimg-put for screenshot/image clipboard transfer to d3-style hosts
description:
Purpose:
Implement the stretch goal in Skillbox: if the operator screenshots on the laptop, they need a practical way to make that image available inside a remote terminal/chat session. The proven approach is not true binary paste through a terminal; it is local macOS clipboard image extraction, upload to the remote target, and putting the remote path back on the Mac clipboard so it can be pasted into a terminal chat.

Current proven behavior from devl:
- Reads PNG from NSPasteboard directly, falling back to TIFF conversion through AppKit/NSBitmapImageRep.
- Supports targets d/default, s/Sweet Potato, j/Jeremy, and c/Conference direct WSL.
- Uploads to `/home/<user>/clipboard-images/clipboard-<timestamp>.png`.
- Verifies the file is non-empty with remote `file` in proof runs.
- Copies the remote path back to the Mac clipboard.
- Restores previous text clipboard in tests/proofs.

Requested work:
Move this helper into Skillbox, align target resolution with Skillbox host metadata, and decide the command name. Keep the command honest in docs: it transfers an image file and returns a path; it does not magically make arbitrary remote terminal paste consume image bytes. Consider optional future sugar such as emitting Markdown image syntax, a `--print-only` flag, or `--open`/`--cat-command` suggestions, but keep the first version tight.

Acceptance criteria:
- macOS-only behavior is explicit and fails cleanly on non-Darwin systems.
- Target mapping uses the same direct `conference1-wsl` rule as text clipboard support.
- Generic `user@host` mode works or is explicitly deferred with a follow-up bead.
- Remote directory handling does not create literal `~/...` paths under the remote home; tilde expansion must normalize to absolute paths before scp/SFTP upload.
- Tests cover no-image clipboard error, PNG/TIFF extraction command construction, target mapping, and tilde normalization.
- Live proof uploads a PNG to d, s, j, and c targets and verifies remote `file` output.

Validation:
- `bash -n` on the helper.
- Local synthetic 1x1 PNG clipboard test with remote verification.
- No local clipboard contents are left mutated after proof runs.

title: Document clipboard bootstrap, d3 usage, proof commands, and agent handoff guidance
description:
Purpose:
Future agents should not need to rediscover the copy/paste architecture from transcripts. Document how to use it, how to bootstrap it on new hosts, and how to debug failures.

Docs to update or create:
- README or docs/operations clipboard section for operator-facing usage.
- AGENTS.md or generated agent context for agent-facing do/don't guidance.
- Host adoption/runbook docs for new d3-style servers.
- Troubleshooting docs for common failures.

Required content:
- Text copy usage: `printf ... | clipcopy`, tmux copy-mode y/Enter/mouse drag, and remote pbcopy compatibility shim.

title: Resolve critical disk pressure before broad validation
description:
Reality check: the broad unittest lane hit `No space left on device` once, and local pressure remained critical after partial temporary cleanup. Broad validation cannot be trusted while the machine may fail tests or generated artifacts from ENOSPC.

Fix direction: start with read-only pressure inventory, protect declared runtime/secret state, then either recover enough local free space for the broad suite or route broad validation through an approved offloaded path.
design:
writes:
  - none
stop_rules:
  - If free space is insufficient and no offload path is already approved, record the blocker instead of deleting data.
non_goals:
  - Do not perform Docker prune, cache deletion, or ballast changes from this node.
global_constraints:
  - Read-only by default; no deletion/truncation/moves without explicit operator approval.
  - Never touch protected agent history or secrets: ~/.codex, ~/.claude, .env, .env.box, workspace/secrets, client overlays.
  - Do not commit; integration lead owns final commit decision.

Done when:
* pressure-report and/or disk-space-triage inventory is recorded.
* Protected paths are not deleted, truncated, or moved.
* There is enough local free space for broad validation, or an approved offload/skip blocker is recorded.
* No cleanup is performed without explicit approval where deletion is involved.

title: DECISION: repository license / legal posture (operator input required)
description:
DECISION: Choose and publish the repository's license / legal posture. OPERATOR INPUT REQUIRED — agents must not select a license unilaterally.

BACKGROUND: README Limitations states "No license file is included yet"; the repo is public-ish ("opensource/skillbox" path, public install.sh curl instructions targeting github.com/build000r/skillbox) while README's contribution section says outside contributions are not accepted. Without a license, default copyright applies: users technically may not copy/modify/redistribute — which contradicts the public installer story and creates ambiguity for anyone the operator invites (shared-jam collaborators).

OPTIONS TO PRESENT (with consequences, for the operator to choose): (a) MIT/Apache-2.0 — maximal adoption, others may fork/commercialize; Apache adds a patent grant. (b) PolyForm Noncommercial / BSL-style source-available — public reading + personal use, no commercial competition; not OSI open source, some users will pass. (c) AGPL-3.0 — open source with strong copyleft; commercial users mostly self-exclude. (d) Explicit all-rights-reserved notice — honest closed posture; the installer story should then say "source-visible, not open source". The no-outside-contributions stance is compatible with ALL options (license != contribution policy) but pairs naturally with (b)/(d); if (a)/(c), consider a CONTRIBUTING.md formalizing "PRs reviewed for illustration, not merged" as README already sketches.

EXECUTION ONCE DECIDED: add LICENSE file (or NOTICE for option d), README badge/section update, remove the Limitations line, note in CHANGELOG; if source-available, audit install.sh/docs wording for "open source" claims and correct them.

ACCEPTANCE: (1) operator decision recorded HERE with date and rationale; (2) LICENSE/NOTICE committed; (3) README + install docs consistent with the choice; (4) Limitations entry removed.

RISKS: none technical; the only failure mode is an agent "helpfully" picking one — hence this is type-decision and blocks nothing else in the plan.

MAINTAINER NOTES: This bead deliberately has no dependencies and nothing depends on it: the legal gap is real but must not bottleneck engineering. Surface it to the operator at the next session touching docs.
close_reason: Operator decision 2026-06-21: keep all-rights-reserved / no OSI license. README posture beads in the docs epic to state this explicitly.

title: Onboarding demo: examples/first-box-demo.md with captured expected outputs
description:
OBJECTIVE: A runnable onboarding demo — examples/first-box-demo.md walking zero-to-focused-client on a local checkout with a public sample repo, every command paired with its expected output — doubling as a manual acceptance script for the first-box flow.

(4) Honest timing notes (sync clones skill repos — first run is minutes). (5) Cross-link from README quickstart and docs/clients.md (coordinate with the README-restructure bead; whichever lands second wires links). FILES: examples/first-box-demo.md (new), possibly a tiny public demo-app repo (operator action — flag in PR if created), README/docs links.

RISKS: output drift making the doc lie (the dated-capture convention + normalization bounds it; the demo is also the natural victim-first artifact when CLI output changes — acceptable, even desirable as a drift alarm); blueprint defaults changing (pin the blueprint name + --set keys used).

ACCEPTANCE: (1) a fresh operator (or agent) following the doc verbatim on a clean checkout reaches a curl-able demo service; (2) cleanup restores doctor-green pristine state; (3) every output block from a real captured run, dated; (4) linked from README quickstart; (5) re-running the demo after cleanup works (idempotency of the walkthrough).

Skillbox's operator and agent control plane remains truthful under provider failure, concurrent mutation, wrapper drift, and partial health, while faster brain reads improve correct decisions rather than amplifying unsafe guidance.

Root success contract:
- SC-1 Truthful destructive lifecycle. Outcome: destructive transitions advance only from typed, observed provider evidence and every advertised teardown surface can satisfy the CLI confirmation contract. Evidence: focused lifecycle/provider regression tests distinguish found, confirmed-not-found, retryable/permanent failure, and malformed responses; Make and MCP argv golden tests prove confirmation forwarding. Failure avoided: auth/network/rate-limit failures being recorded as confirmed destruction, or wrappers advertising a teardown they can never execute.
- SC-2 Single-mutator discipline. Outcome: one state-root writer lock covers the documented public mutation boundaries and pulse while reads and true dry-runs remain available. Evidence: coverage inventory plus tests for mutual exclusion, nested ownership, timeout metadata, crash release, multiple roots, and read/dry-run availability. Failure avoided: concurrent humans, swarms, or pulse corrupting multi-step invariants.
- SC-3 Executable command contract. Outcome: a lint-first ratchet compares live CLI, registry, MCP, Make, aliases, safety forwarding, risk, and side-effect declarations; CI rejects new drift while a checked-in baseline can only shrink. Evidence: the repaired teardown contract is the first golden and synthetic drift tests fail deterministically. Failure avoided: descriptive metadata and duplicated wrappers silently diverging again.
- SC-4 Quality-first guidance and health. Outcome: a 15–20 scenario redacted Brain Quality Lab checks grounding, acceptable actions, forbidden actions, and abstention; a federated read-only doctor exposes stable IDs, scope, severity, freshness, provenance, unavailable/timed-out states, and one prioritized next action. Evidence: reproducible corpus results plus provider contract/integration tests and bounded runtime. Failure avoided: faster or broader automation confidently recommending the wrong action, and fresh agents guessing which validator to run.
- SC-5 Measured brain acceleration. Outcome: cold startup, model construction, graph work, and adapters are profiled; independent adapters use bounded parallelism only where evidence supports it; any cache decision is conditional and limited to a sanitized, versioned brain projection. Evidence: stable non-flaky latency proof and no regression in SC-4 quality outcomes. Failure avoided: optimizing an unknown bottleneck or persisting secret-adjacent resolved state.
- SC-6 Integrated release proof. Outcome: all branches converge through focused and broad validation, docs/operations updates, rollback notes, and detached fresh-eyes review before completion. Evidence: repo-native test/lint/doctor/dev-sanity/brain proof outputs, clean diff, committed Beads, and reviewer findings resolved or explicitly blocked. Failure avoided: locally correct components shipping as an incoherent control plane.

Non-goals:
- No full digital-twin simulator, generic shell-backed doctor --fix, locks --clear verb, raw persistent resolved-model cache, universal receipt framework, built-in SigV4 backup transport, or five-source causal timeline.
- Do not merge command registries unless the ratchet proves that consolidation is still valuable.
- Do not provision, destroy, enroll, or mutate live infrastructure for proof.

Constraints and authority:
- Preserve local/user state and secrets; standard-library-first; structured compact CLI/MCP output; Tailnet-only exposure rules.
- Codex gpt-5.6-sol max owns planning, architecture, impactful safety work, integration acceptance, and final say (max for all planning, implementation, integration, and final review). Fable 5 High is the bounded execution challenger and reviewer for hydrated leaves; gpt-5.6-sol max retains pivotal and final authority.
- Final authority: Codex root planning/integration authority after detached fresh-context review.
design: Synthesis topology: five deferred grouping branches own lifecycle truth, single-mutator discipline, command ratchet, quality-health, and brain performance. Hydrated execution leaves flow into lifecycle and mutation branch integrations, then one global integration and one detached final review. Planning hierarchy is carried by canonical notes, never parent dependency edges; only implementation ordering uses blocking edges. Priority frontier begins with independent P0 lifecycle provider truth and teardown surface parity plus P1 mutation inventory, health protocol, quality corpus, and component profile. Root arbitration: lifecycle owns Make-MCP-box behavior; mutation owns canonical boundary IDs and kernel lease; command contract references those IDs and owns parity/CI diagnostics; command CI owns workflow edits until mutation integration follows; performance cannot land before the quality corpus. Shared-file collisions are serialized by explicit dependencies. Stable mutation lock lives beside the canonical resolved state root so restore cannot replace it. All infrastructure proof is mocked or read-only. Dueling authority: gpt-5.6-sol max owns safety architecture, pivotal implementation, integration, and final acceptance; Fable 5 High owns adversarial inventory, hostile matrices, and fresh review; bounded Fable 5 High execution is permitted only after divide-and-conquer validates a hydrated ready leaf.

title: Implement the authoritative reentrant state-root mutation lease
description: Outcome: a resolved state root has one kernel-flock writer lease with truthful post-acquisition metadata, explicit nested ownership, bounded waits, and crash-safe release. Evidence: process-level mutual exclusion, crash, nesting, timeout, stale metadata, and distinct-root tests. Failure avoided: metadata being mistaken for authority or per-file locks permitting cross-file invariant interleaving.
design: Exact writes: .env-manager/runtime_manager/state_mutation.py; tests/test_state_mutation_lock.py new; .env-manager/runtime_manager/_shared/errors.py only if structured error plumbing cannot remain local. Acquire LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB on a stable sibling path derived from state_root.resolve, never inside the root because restore renames the root. Use bounded wait, non-inheritable descriptor, and fail closed when flock is unavailable. Explicit StateMutationLease is required for nested owners; same-root nesting reuses it, cross-root nesting is rejected or deterministically ordered. Metadata is advisory, redacted, written only after acquisition, and cleared or replaced only while holding the kernel lock; never unlink the lock and never expose clear. Timeout includes canonical root, boundary and operation IDs, waited duration, lock path, and best-effort holder pid/start/command. Non-goals: no distributed lease, stealing, heartbeat, or read lock. Model route: gpt-5.6-sol max. Review owner: fresh Fable 5 High adversarial safety review. Final authority: Codex root. Stop condition: any unsupported flock, ambiguous canonical root, unsafe descriptor inheritance, or metadata behavior that could authorize ownership fails closed and blocks adoption.

title: Lube: auto-sync beads on git commit to eliminate per-session br sync ceremony
description:
CASS evidence: 120+ sessions contain manual 'br sync --flush-only' invocations across 500 recent sessions. Every session that touches beads ends with the same 3-step ceremony: br sync --flush-only, git add .beads/, git commit. This is pure mechanical friction.

No-ragrets success contract:
- Outcome: a pre-commit hook auto-runs 'br sync --flush-only' when .beads/beads.db exists, so agents never type the sync command manually
- Evidence: grep across 50 future sessions shows zero manual 'br sync --flush-only' invocations
- Failure avoided: agents forgetting to sync beads before commit, stale .beads/issues.jsonl diverging from SQLite

Lube unblocker: add a pre-commit hook (or git hook template) in the skillbox repo that detects .beads/beads.db and runs br sync --flush-only automatically. The hook should be idempotent, fast (<2s), and silent on success. Install it via make bootstrap-env or a dedicated make install-hooks target.
notes: Included in no-ragrets high-use weak-surface slate skillbox-high-use-weak-surfaces-no-ragrets-fxm8. User agreed this is a future pass candidate: remove repeated manual br sync ceremony while preserving explicit git staging/commit review.

title: Lube: pre-load common deferred tools in settings to eliminate ToolSearch round-trips
description:
CASS evidence: 20% of interactive sessions call ToolSearch at least once (5/25 sessions). Common deferred tools (TaskCreate, TaskUpdate, TaskGet, WebSearch, WebFetch, Monitor) require agents to call ToolSearch before first use, adding a wasted round-trip per session. The system-reminder lists these tools every turn but their schemas aren't loaded until explicitly fetched.

This is architectural (how Claude Code defers tool schemas for context efficiency), but the permission/settings system may offer a way to pre-load the most frequently needed tools.

No-ragrets success contract:
- Outcome: the 5 most commonly needed deferred tools are either pre-loaded or agents know to batch-load them in the first turn, reducing wasted ToolSearch calls from ~1.2/session to <0.3/session.
- Evidence: sessions that use TaskCreate/TaskUpdate no longer show a preceding ToolSearch call; or AGENTS.md includes a one-line startup instruction to pre-load common tools.
- Failure avoided: agents losing one tool-call round-trip per session to schema loading, or worse, agents not using task tracking because the ceremony to load it is too high.

Lube unblocker: investigate whether .claude/settings.json can pre-load tool schemas, or add a one-line AGENTS.md instruction ("call ToolSearch for TaskCreate,TaskUpdate,WebSearch in your first turn if you need them"). Smallest fix: AGENTS.md guidance. Better fix: settings-level pre-load if supported.
close_reason: AGENTS.md gains a 'Deferred Tools' section instructing agents to batch-load common deferred tools (TaskCreate, TaskUpdate, WebSearch, WebFetch, Monitor) with one ToolSearch select:... call in the first turn instead of per-tool round-trips (commit 7a0b3b7). Settings-level pre-load investigated: Claude Code settings.json has no supported key to force-load deferred tool schemas — deferral is harness-architectural; AGENTS.md guidance is the available fix, matching the bead's 'smallest fix' contract.

title: Lube: auto-clear stale index-run.lock from dead cass indexer PIDs
description:
CASS evidence: 64 hits for agents encountering stale index-run.lock files from dead indexer PIDs. Experienced directly in this session: PID 125188 died but left lock behind, causing cass status/health to report stale and blocking subsequent cass operations. Agents had to manually identify the dead PID, confirm it was not running, and remove the lock files.

No-ragrets success contract:
- Outcome: sbp cass status auto-detects stale locks (PID dead per os.kill(pid, 0)), clears them, and reports the cleared lock in the payload. No manual intervention needed.
- Evidence: direct experience in this session + 64 cass hits showing the same pattern across sessions.
- Failure avoided: agents spending tool calls diagnosing a phantom lock, manually clearing files, and retrying operations.
- Acceptance: (1) dead PID locks are auto-cleared before health probes, (2) live PID locks are left alone, (3) cleared lock info is included in the status payload for transparency, (4) 12/12 tests pass including 2 new stale-lock tests.
close_reason: Fix applied: _clear_stale_index_lock() in sbp_cass.py auto-detects dead PIDs via os.kill(pid, 0) and clears lock+meta files. 12/12 tests pass.

title: grok transcode derives cwd from the session-name prefix and dumps 2744 of 3539 sessions into workspace /tmp
description:
Measured 2026-07-25 while implementing skillbox-vev1 (skillbox-config 3770799): the grok transcode path derives each session's cwd from the session-NAME prefix rather than a recorded cwd, and 2744 of 3539 grok sessions land in workspace '/tmp'.

Since cass attributes workspace solely from the cwd field (proven in vev1's controlled sandbox), every one of those sessions is unreachable via --workspace <repo> and pollutes /tmp aggregation instead.

Together with skillbox-cass-unindexed-sidechains-*, this is what actually caps live per-repo friction mining — for the skillbox repo only 45 conversations carry the workspace (26 restored + 18 grok-cli + 1 codex).

Fix: derive grok cwd from a recorded field if one exists in the raw transcript; if none exists, leave workspace NULL rather than asserting /tmp, so the data is honestly missing instead of wrong.

title: Epic: invisible Oracle Pro subagent across local, d3, and d3c
description: Future vantage point: asking an agent to escalate to GPT Pro feels identical to asking for a normal subagent. No visible browser, manual tab selection, prompt copy, polling ritual, or per-machine login choreography. SC-1 Invisible local execution: one stable command launches a proven GPT Pro or Deep Research run invisibly (hidden-headful when true headless is Cloudflare-blocked) and returns a structured receipt. SC-2 Durable auth: browser state lives in one explicit least-privilege profile, never in repo artifacts, with health and re-auth diagnostics that do not expose cookies. SC-3 Fleet reach: d3 and d3c can invoke the trusted auth host over an authenticated Tailnet route without copying browser cookies across machines. SC-4 Truthful lifecycle: submitted, started, completed, failed, and timed-out are distinct; completion requires captured assistant output and model/tool proof. SC-5 Subagent ergonomics: callers pass prompt, files, slug, result path, and wait policy through a narrow CLI contract; default output is quiet and machine-readable. SC-6 Native destination: the proven standalone path is absorbed into opensource/skillbox as a supervised capability with install, doctor, status, logs, and teardown. Failure avoided: silent Instant fallback, visible Chrome, leaked cookies, duplicate runs, ambiguous tabs, and fake completion. Non-goals: no API-key spend, no raw cookie copying to d3/d3c, no weakening fail-closed model/tool verification, and no dependency on a human watching a browser. Constraints: preserve current Oracle result quality; use live Oracle capabilities where reliable; keep secrets outside git; Tailnet/private transport only; local reversible implementation may precede the native Skillbox absorption. Final authority: Codex root after executable proof and fresh review.
design:
Audience map
- Operator: invokes Pro/Deep Research like a normal subagent and sees only a result/receipt.
- Calling agents and skills: use a narrow deterministic command/MCP contract, never browser choreography.
- d3 and d3c clients: submit prompt/files to the trusted auth host without owning cookies or CDP.
- Maintainer: gets install/auth/doctor/status/logs/down, typed failures, fixtures, and live proof.

Surface map
escalate route -> deep-research prompt construction -> oracle-subagent CLI -> trusted hidden browser/controller -> receipt/result.
Later: d3/d3c client -> authenticated loopback tunnel/relay -> trusted host worker.
Final: sbp oracle and MCP mirror supervise the same contract.

Architecture decisions
1. True Chrome headless is not accepted: live smoke reached Cloudflare challenge and stayed blocked. Steady state is headful Chrome launched off-screen/background and immediately hidden; one-time auth login may be deliberately visible.
2. One canonical 0700 profile lives only on the trusted auth host. No rsync clone, cookie JSON, inline cookie transport, or CDP exposure.
3. Oracle is initially a renderer/low-level adapter, not lifecycle authority. Current native headless, statuses, and remote server are insufficient.
4. One run binds exact target, baseline turn identity, model/tool proof, submission, start signal, new assistant output, and atomic result hash.
5. Raw oracle serve is forbidden at the fleet boundary because it accepts broad browserConfig/pre-submit hooks. Fleet RPC is an allowlisted schema inside authenticated Tailnet/SSH transport.
6. Standalone CLI is proven first. Native Skillbox absorption preserves its receipt/state contract.

Thirty-idea inventory
01 hidden persistent browser supervisor; 02 truthful lifecycle receipts; 03 one-command CLI; 04 auth login/doctor; 05 restricted fleet RPC; 06 exact model/tool proof; 07 Pro/Deep Research adapters; 08 idempotent reattach; 09 durable queue/tab leases; 10 secret-safe artifacts/events; 11 performance SLO; 12 DOM/fake-CDP fixtures; 13 local live matrix; 14 d3/d3c dogfood; 15 native Skillbox absorption; 16 cancel/resume; 17 exact result cache; 18 multiple accounts; 19 crash recovery; 20 Chrome canary; 21 Oracle feature probe; 22 attachment limits (promoted to required SC-3 gate after global review); 23 provenance; 24 auth encryption study; 25 completion callbacks; 26 metrics; 27 follow-up turns; 28 Windows auth-host failover; 29 caller policy/quota; 30 timeline view.

Launch signal
Ask for a Pro escalation from Codex, d3, or d3c and get a normal subagent-style result: no visible browser, no copy/paste, no Chrome babysitting. Auth lives once on the trusted browser host; every run returns a URL, model/tool proof, result, and receipt.

Hard distrust gates
Any visible/focus-stealing browser in steady state; silent Instant/model/tool drift; copied cookies/profile/token; ambiguous tab; stale assistant output counted as this run; completed without atomic nonempty result; wildcard listener; raw remote hook execution.
acceptance_criteria:
SC-1 Invisible local execution
- One stable command runs Pro or Deep Research with no visible/focused browser.
- Live Cloudflare-compatible hidden-headful proof, exact target/model/tool evidence, cold/warm timing, and one persistent profile/PID reuse evidence.

SC-2 Durable auth
- Profile path/owner/mode, authenticated identity/project/Pro probe, explicit NEEDS_REAUTH, and one-time login path are proven.
- Negative audit finds no cookie/profile/token in git, run artifacts, argv, logs, d3, or d3c.

SC-3 Fleet reach
- Authenticated private d3 and canonical d3c->conference1-wsl invocations return file-backed results.
- Wrong identity/token, replay, tunnel loss, oversized/forbidden fields fail before browser contact; no wildcard listener or raw CDP.

SC-4 Truthful lifecycle
- submitted requires a new user turn/conversation binding after baseline.
- started requires a new run-bound progress/assistant signal.
- completed requires new assistant output, cleared active state, atomic result write, byte count/hash, and valid model/tool proof.
- timeout, cancellation, delivery failure, browser death, stale prior output, and ambiguous targets never become completed.

SC-5 Subagent ergonomics
- Stable CLI supports mode, prompt/stdin/file, attachments, slug, result, wait, timeout, JSON, status, and reattach.
- Default stdout is compact machine JSON; diagnostics/events are durable and secret-safe.
- Identical concurrent calls send once and share a receipt; distinct calls queue/lease safely.

SC-6 Native destination
- Proven contract becomes pinned supervised sbp oracle install/auth/up/doctor/status/logs/down/consult plus MCP mirror.
- Lifecycle is dry-run-first where mutating, loopback/private only, redacted, and executable through local/d3/d3c proof.

Final close gate
All six SCs have executable evidence, no open P0/P1 descendant blocks the release, two consecutive independent fresh review scores >=850/1000 against the same graph/proof SHA, and root synthesis receipt names every proof artifact and residual limitation.

title: Auth doctor read GUEST data: backend-api probes omitted the bearer
description:
VERIFIED 2026-07-28. oracle-subagent-auth.mjs readJson() called /backend-api/me, /accounts/check/v4-2023-04-27 and /models with credentials:'include' and NO Authorization header. backend-api authenticates by BEARER, not cookie, so all three returned HTTP 200 describing a GUEST. Measured on the live authenticated session:
  cookie-only: plan_type=guest, 5 model slugs
  bearer:      plan_type=pro,  19 slugs incl gpt-5-6-pro, research
It failed OPEN - a Pro account looked free, and gpt-5-6-pro/research vanished.

CONSEQUENCE 1: the doctor's Pro verification fell back entirely to DOM evidence (profileProAvailable / button text 'pro'), so the system's headline claim of proving Pro at the DOM level was not corroborated by any API signal - it WAS the only signal.

CONSEQUENCE 2 (worse): /backend-api/me returns a DIFFERENT id with cookies-only vs bearer (hash 75a38e2f... vs e26c639c..., verified non-matching). The enrollment minted 2026-07-28T22:32 recorded account_fingerprint from the GUEST identity. The 'immutable account identity, no use-whichever-account-is-open fallback' guarantee was therefore pinned to an anonymous session and was vacuous.

FIX APPLIED: readJson now fetches /api/auth/session for the accessToken and sends Authorization: Bearer on all three probes. Unit suite 305/305 green.
