title: Pro plan never proven: 'default' account alias broke the length===1 test
description:
VERIFIED + FIXED 2026-07-28. deriveAccountCapability (oracle-subagent-auth.mjs) computed uniquePro = proAccounts.length === 1 ? proAccounts[0] : null. ChatGPT's /backend-api/accounts/check returns the SAME account twice - once keyed by its account UUID and once by the literal alias 'default' - with an IDENTICAL account_id (verified: matching account_id on both, both plan_type=pro, can_access_with_session=true, has_active_subscription=true, is_delinquent=false). So length was 2, uniquePro was null, selectedAccount was null, and pro_plan was FALSE for a genuine Pro account. The accessible.length===1 fallback failed for the same reason.

This is the same fail-closed 'exactly one match' cardinality trap that pervades the DOM layer (composer_ambiguous, model_control_ambiguous, send_control_ambiguous), here applied to an API response.

FIX: collapse aliases by account_id/organization_id/account_user_id before the uniqueness test, preferring the concrete map key so workspace identity never becomes the string 'default'.

RESULT: doctor went from reasons=['auth_policy_missing','pro_plan_missing'] to pro_plan:true. Enrollment then SUCCEEDED for the first time: ok:true state:ready, all 17 checks green. The new account_fingerprint differs from the guest-derived one, confirming hjuc.10. Suite 317/317.

title: Answers land in root chat, not the Project; add cheap instant lane
description:
FIXED + VERIFIED 2026-07-28. Two root causes:
(1) connectCdp preferred a '/c/' conversation tab over the Project page. Every ask leaves a /c/ tab behind, so from the second ask onward the sentinel template was harvested from a conversation page and the Project binding was lost.
(2) The Project binding is carried by conversation_mode = {kind:'gizmo_interaction', gizmo_id:'g-p-<project>'} in the POST body. buildConversationBody inherited whatever the drifted tab had, and also inherited that tab's conversation_id, which would append to the old chat rather than start one in the Project.

FIX: projectIdFromUrl() accepts a Project URL or bare g-p-id; connectCdp prefers the Project page when one is configured; buildConversationBody sets conversation_mode explicitly and drops the inherited conversation_id when a projectId is given. New --project flag on oracle-ask plus ORACLE_CHATGPT_PROJECT_URL default, and a 'filing into <id>' progress line.

VERIFIED AT THE SOURCE, not from the log line: GET /backend-api/gizmos/<g-p-id>/conversations went 0 -> 1 -> 2, both conversations carrying the gizmo_id.

CHEAP TESTING LANE: --model instant (gpt-5-5-instant) already existed and is now documented as the testing default - measured 6.7-7.2s vs 27.4s for Pro, and it does not consume the Pro allowance. SKILL.md updated with both.

4 regression tests added (alias binding, no inherited conversation_id, non-project passthrough, URL parsing). Suite 323/323. Also cleaned 10 leaked page targets down to 1 parked on the Project.
notes:
FOLLOW-UP BUG FOUND + FIXED 2026-07-28: inline (fast-model) answers were TRUNCATED after their first chunk. summariseConversationStream handled only two frame shapes - the opening 'add' message and an explicit append naming /message/content/parts/0 - but delta_encoding v1 then sends the bulk of the answer as bare {"v":"..."} continuation frames with NO p and NO o, because the path is already implied. Captured from a live gpt-5-5-instant stream: 1 add + 1 explicit append + 6-8 bare continuation frames + 1 patch. All bare frames were dropped, so answers ended mid-sentence and read like model terseness rather than a bug.

FIX: track activePath, opened by an assistant/recipient-all message or an explicit /parts/ append; bare {v:string} frames continue that path; o:'patch' arrays are walked for /parts/ appends. A tool-authored delta must NOT open the path or Pro's pre-handoff frames would be glued into the answer - covered by test.

Only fast models were affected. Pro was always correct because its answer arrives via the polling path (extractFinalAnswer), not inline - which is why this hid until instant became the testing default.

3 regression tests from the captured shapes. Suite 326/326. Verified live: full multi-sentence answer via sbp oracle --model instant.

title: Ask must open a FRESH thread by default; continuing is opt-in
description:
FIXED + VERIFIED 2026-07-28. askOracle passed bundle.template.conversation_id straight into the body, so every ask appended to whatever thread the donor CDP tab happened to be sitting on. The earlier Project fix only dodged this by accident: connectCdp started preferring the /project page, whose template usually carries no conversation_id. Behaviour was therefore luck, not contract.

FIX: buildConversationBody never inherits the template's conversation_id - a fresh thread is the default and continuing requires an explicit conversationId. askOracle takes conversationId (default null). oracle-ask gains --continue/--resume (reuse last thread), --conversation <id> (explicit), and --new (explicit default). Last thread recorded at ~/.oracle/oracle-subagent/last-conversation.json (0600, dir 0700), written best-effort so a failure to record never loses an answer already in hand. --continue with no remembered thread is a usage ERROR, never a silent new chat. Progress line now says 'new thread in <project>' vs 'continued thread in <project>'.

Also fixed: UsageError raised after arg parsing fell through the top-level catch to 'unexpected error' with the failure exit code instead of the usage code.

VERIFIED LIVE: ask1 thread 6a695dc2, ask2 thread 6a695dd0 (different -> fresh default), ask3 --continue reused 6a695dd0 AND the model correctly recalled the prior turn ('You asked about an underrated failure mode in retry logic for flaky APIs') - semantic continuity, not just id match. Project listing at 5 conversations, all gizmo-bound.

Suite 327/327. Two pre-existing tests asserted the old inherit-the-thread behaviour and were updated to the new intent rather than worked around.

title: Pro answers returned mid-flight: end_turn is not a completion signal
description:
REPORTED BY OPERATOR 2026-07-28 ('Pro requests ARE NOT FINISHED until that stop square button stops... if they are finished, can't stop. thats probably a better indicator'). CONFIRMED by live capture.

extractFinalAnswer selected the first assistant/all text message with status=finished_successfully AND end_turn=true AND a model_slug. On Pro that fires LONG before generation ends. Live gpt-5-6-pro capture:
  t+0s   async_status=3  extract=no
  t+21s  async_status=3  extract=no
  t+32s  async_status=3  extract=YES(189ch)   <- reported as the answer
  t+73s  async_status=3  extract=YES(189ch)   <- web.run tool still status=in_progress
Re-polled minutes later: STILL async_status=3 with a message in_progress. So a 189-char interim fragment was being returned as the final Pro answer while the real reply had not been produced.

ROOT CAUSE: end_turn/finished_successfully describe a MESSAGE, not the TURN. Pro publishes an interim end_turn text message while tools keep running. The operator's framing is the correct one: the question is 'is the turn still generating', which is what the composer's stop button reflects.

FIX: new turnInProgress(conversation) gate, checked BEFORE extraction in the poll loop. Two independent signals, either meaning still-generating: (1) conversation.async_status === 3 (observed in-progress value), (2) any message with status === 'in_progress'. The pair covers the gap between messages where nothing is individually in progress. Progress line now distinguishes 'still generating' from 'waiting for the answer'.

Deliberately NOT gated on a guessed terminal async_status value - only the observed in-progress value is trusted, so unknown future codes fall through to the in_progress check rather than being misread as still-running.

4 regression tests from the captured mid-flight shape. Suite 331/331.

CONSEQUENCE: earlier Pro timings reported today (12.6s, 27.4s) are SUSPECT - same defect. The one-word test prompts (SMOOTH/FINAL/PROJECTED) were too short to expose it. Re-verification with a substantial Pro question still required.
notes:
END-TO-END VERIFIED 2026-07-28 on a substantial Pro question via 'sbp oracle --model pro':
  BEFORE (reported earlier today): 28.8s, 189 bytes - an interim fragment
  AFTER:  211.9s, 10290 bytes - 210 lines / 1453 words, coherent and complete
Progress line showed 'still generating' repeatedly through the window where the old code would have bailed at ~32s. Filed as a new thread in the Project.

Note on the earlier 15270-char figure: that was a different question. The point stands - the gate now waits for the turn instead of the first finished-looking message.

title: Browser receipt read/write race: unlink-then-write window yields spurious browser_receipt_invalid
description:
Observed live 2026-08-06 during the .6.3/.6.13 proof wave with several concurrent readers: 'node oracle-subagent-auth.mjs status --json' flaps between state=ready reasons=[] and state=blocked reasons=['browser_receipt_invalid'] seconds apart, while the on-disk receipt is complete and valid (schema oracle-subagent.browser.v1, state ready, all 28 required keys present). oracle-session-heal.mjs reports ok:true healed:false because it samples a good moment.

ROOT CAUSE: launch-chatgpt-cdp.sh rewrites the receipt by os.unlink(receipt) then fsync(dir) then write (see the python heredoc around the 'os.unlink(receipt)' line). That is a delete-then-create window, not an atomic replace. Any concurrent reader in oracle-subagent-auth.mjs normalizeBrowserReceipt() sees a missing/partial file, fails isPlainObject(), and gateErrors browser_receipt_invalid.

IMPACT: false NOT-READY on a genuinely healthy authenticated session; agents may 'heal', relaunch, or abort a good run. Worse under concurrency (multi-pane swarms, fleet RPC + local ask at once).

FIX: write to a sibling temp file in the same directory with 0600, fsync the file, then os.replace() onto browser.json, then fsync the directory. Readers should additionally retry once on ENOENT/parse failure before declaring browser_receipt_invalid. Add a concurrency regression test: N parallel status readers during a launcher rewrite must never observe browser_receipt_invalid.

validation: loop 'auth status --json' 20x while a launcher rewrite runs; zero browser_receipt_invalid results. supports: SC-4.

title: Reconstruct ChatGPT backend conversation API from authenticated session
description:
Apply interface-reconstruction api mode. Capture transport for one real submission via CDP Network domain, document the request graph (endpoint, headers, body schema, SSE framing, completion terminator), and build a minimal replayable Node client that submits one Pro question over HTTPS with zero DOM selectors.
supports: PC-http-1
produces: references/chatgpt-backend-api.md + assets/scripts/oracle-http-client.mjs

notes:
CLOSED 2026-07-28. HTTP client WORKS, proven live: oracle-http-client.mjs --model gpt-5-6-pro returned 'HTTP_OK' in 12.6s end-to-end. Model selection is now the JSON field 'model' instead of a dropdown click. Zero ChatGPT CSS selectors (audited: only match in the file is a comment; sole DOM touch is generic HTML button[type=submit] inside a form). 33/33 fixture tests green; full suite 305/305.

HONEST CAVEAT - a fully standalone client is NOT achievable in bounds. /backend-api/f/conversation requires three per-request sentinel headers (chat-requirements, proof, turnstile) minted by executing obfuscated server-shipped challenge programs + SHA-PoW. Forging = reverse-engineering a bot defense, explicitly out of bounds and NOT attempted. In-bounds solution built and proved: the operator's own browser mints a genuine triple, the client intercepts-and-REJECTS the app's outgoing POST so tokens are minted but never spent, then reuses that unused triple. Evidence ladder replayed: no sentinel -> 403 unusual activity; sentinel without cookies -> 403 edge interstitial; sentinel + cookies -> 200 text/event-stream.

So the browser stays as a token/PoW source but is no longer the worker. Pro turns do not answer on the POST: initial stream emits stream_handoff and DONE after ~4s, answer arrives via resume channel; client polls GET /backend-api/conversation/{id} using the advertised poll_interval_ms. Extraction must filter on metadata.model_slug present - each Pro turn also emits a reasoning_recap message with end_turn:true and no slug, so a naive role+status filter returns the recap. Regression test covers it.

Residual unknowns in the coverage ledger (bounded_proof_complete=false): resume_sse_endpoint URL, WS topic protocol, minimal enforced header subset, Deep Research never submitted, inline-delta path for fast models is inferred only.

title: Configure sigstore identity policy for source-install verification
description: From installer-workmanship pass (m19o.6): maybe_verify_sigstore_bundle in install.sh detects bundles and hard-fails without cosign, but when cosign IS present it only warns that no identity policy is configured, so signatures are never actually verified. Needs the release pipeline to publish .sigstore.json bundles and the installer to pin certificate identity/issuer. Acceptance: with a published bundle, install verifies signature against pinned identity; tampered bundle fails install.
close_reason: Sigstore identity policy pinned. maybe_verify_sigstore_bundle in install.sh now runs 'cosign verify-blob --bundle <path>.sigstore.json --certificate-identity-regexp ^https://github.com/build000r/skillbox/.github/workflows/release.yml@refs/tags/ --certificate-oidc-issuer https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com <artifact>' — a valid bundle signed by the release workflow's OIDC identity verifies; a tampered artifact or untrusted signer makes cosign exit non-zero and install aborts (unless --allow-unverified). Identity/issuer are overridable via SKILLBOX_INSTALL_SIGSTORE_* env for forks. .github/workflows/release.yml signs the tarball keyless (cosign sign-blob, id-token: write) and publishes skillbox-<tag>.tar.gz.sigstore.json; install.sh download_release_assets best-effort fetches that bundle. Tests in tests/test_install_release.py prove pinned-identity flags are invoked (cosign mocked), tampered->fail, and --allow-unverified bypass. bash -n clean; 24/24 install tests pass. HUMAN FOLLOW-UP: cut a tag so the workflow produces a real signed bundle to verify end-to-end (Rekor/Fulcio); keep the pinned identity regexp in sync if the repo/workflow path changes.

title: Lube: default bv --format toon in agent contexts to cut triage token waste
description:
CASS evidence: 12-60% of sessions invoke bv --robot-triage. Sessions that call it without --format toon produce 100KB+ of JSON output that agents must parse, consuming massive context window space. Two of the longest sessions (2.3MB, 815KB) directly correlate with uncompressed bv triage output.

The --format toon option already exists and produces token-optimized output, but agents don't default to it because AGENTS.md documents the bare command first.

No-ragrets success contract:
- Outcome: all agent bv --robot-triage invocations default to --format toon, reducing triage output from ~100KB to <10KB per call.
- Evidence: grep across 30 future sessions shows no bare bv --robot-triage without --format toon; longest-session outliers shrink by >50%.
- Failure avoided: token-heavy triage output pushing agents into context compression mid-task, losing working state; or agents reading only partial triage output and missing findings.

Lube unblocker: update AGENTS.md bv instructions to show --format toon as the default recommended form. Optionally add an agent-detection wrapper (BV_FORMAT_DEFAULT=toon env var or similar) so agents always get TOON unless they explicitly override.
close_reason: AGENTS.md bv documentation now shows --format toon on every --robot-* example (mega-command, next, plan, insights, recipes, workflow step 1) with explicit rationale, verified live: bv --robot-triage --format toon emits 23KB TOON vs 100KB+ JSON; BV_OUTPUT_FORMAT env var documented; TOON renderer dependency (tru crate) and JSON fallback behavior documented. Commit 7a0b3b7.

title: mmdx --tmux can reach npm install without --allow-parser-install, in a detached child after exit
description:
Found by static reading during skillbox-mutation-gap-delegates-cukm (commit 7141769). Not fixed there: the defect lives in the external skill repo build000r-skills/mmdx.

Chain:
1. mmdx_open.py:449-450 appends --no-parser-install unless the operator passes --allow-parser-install. Good.
2. mmd.py:1161-1181 start_handoff_channel spawns the detached --handoff-server child with subprocess.Popen(..., start_new_session=True) and does NOT forward --no-parser-install.
3. Both _handle_source_preflight and _handle_source_write call preflight_source_code(code, source_path) (mmd.py:400-406, 896, 917) with auto_install defaulting to True.

Net: 'manage mmdx --tmux' WITHOUT --allow-parser-install can still reach npm install (mmd.py:1223-1228, cwd=SCRIPT_DIR, target <mmdx skill>/scripts/node_modules), inside a detached grandchild that outlives the command, up to the 600s handoff TTL after it returned.

Live, not theoretical: node_modules/mermaid is absent on this host, so the short-circuit at mmd.py:1211 does not fire.

The operator's explicit refusal to allow a parser install is silently reversed by a code path they cannot see, after the command they ran has already exited.

Two fixes, not exclusive:
- Upstream (correct): forward the parser-install decision to the detached child and honor it in preflight_source_code.
- Local defensive (this repo, mmdx_open.py): refuse --tmux unless --allow-parser-install is explicit, and/or pass an explicit --handoff-ttl. mmdx_open.py was outside cukm's write allowlist.

Cross-reference: manage.mmdx is classified conditional_mutation in the state_mutation manifest with lease_span 'whole_command + BOUNDED 600s detached tail only with --tmux'.

title: Fix up/down dependency graph recovery for unhealthy already-running services
description:
Context: The operator hit `sbp up` from <workspace>/cycle-chef and got spaps + htma_server reported as already-running while the API summary showed both health URLs down. This is not only a Cycle Chef issue; it is an upstream local-runtime dependency graph contract issue for any client overlay using managed services, depends_on, and healthchecks.

Problem: runtime_ops._start_service currently returns already-running as soon as a managed pid file resolves to a live pid. It does this before checking the declared healthcheck. That lets an unhealthy live process satisfy a dependency edge and makes `up` look successful while downstream services start against dead APIs. Text rendering also prints bootstrap task rows as unknown when local-runtime summaries use status instead of result.

Success contract:
- A live pid with a failing declared healthcheck is not treated as successful already-running.
- `up` either repairs the service through the normal declared command path after clearing stale/unhealthy runtime state, or returns a structured failed/blocked result that stops the graph and points to status/logs/restart.
- Healthy pre-existing HTTP/port/process/path services are still reused without spawning duplicates.
- Dependency graph startup does not continue after a dependency fails or times out.
- Text output for bootstrap tasks renders status/result clearly, never harmless unknown for planned/ready/completed rows.

Validation target: focused unittest coverage for runtime_ops/start_services, local-runtime up graph failure behavior, text rendering task rows, plus python3 -m unittest for touched test modules. Link evidence back to skillbox-config runtime normalization bead skillbox-config-sbp-up-runtime-tree-m9z.3.
close_reason: Implemented unhealthy live-pid recovery, dependency blocking, task status rendering, and focused validation; dev-sanity caveat recorded for unrelated stale skill installs.

title: Port guard: five-layer enforcement stack from the June duel
description:
EPIC: Implement the five-layer port-guard stack that the 2026-06-11 dueling-wizards round (Claude Opus, Codex gpt-5.5, Grok — DUELING_WIZARDS_REPORT_PORT_GUARD.md) converged on independently, so dev services can no longer bind wrong ports, auto-hop, or accumulate as rogue listeners.

PROBLEM EVIDENCE: at duel time the live box showed four duplicate Vite servers (5173/5174/5176/5177), one on 0.0.0.0 violating tailnet_only posture. Agents bypass `sbp up` with direct `npm run dev`; Vite silently auto-increments ports.

CONSENSUS BUILD ORDER (verbatim from the duel): Phase 0 port registry (foundation, "not a ranked idea, a prerequisite") -> Phase 1 dev-command intercept via PATH shims + PreToolUse hook (avg score 810) -> Phase 2 post-bind verification in service start (763-845) -> Phase 3 pulse rogue-listener sentinel (745-795, only layer covering ALL bypass paths) -> Phase 4 repo port contracts (.skillbox-port.env + strictPort, 585-628) -> Phase 5 optional eBPF cage, DEFERRED behind telemetry.

KILLED IDEAS — do not resurrect: nftables port cage (filters packets, not bind(); formally retracted by two models), LD_PRELOAD bind guard (trivially bypassed), proxy-owned canonical ports (masks the problem; contradicts the 2026-06-04 port-per-app pivot).

SUCCESS CRITERIA (Grok, endorsed 3-way): (1) `npm run dev` in tmux blocked in one turn with the exact runtime command; (2) full-path bypass crashes on strictPort or is reaped within one pulse interval; (3) no silent port hops; (4) no multi-day rogue accumulation; (5) no surviving 0.0.0.0 dev listeners under tailnet_only.

Exit: all five criteria encoded as automated regression tests and passing; telemetry counters inform the Phase-5 decision bead.
close_reason: All five port-guard layers and the regression/telemetry proof bead are implemented, verified, and pushed.

title: Port registry: derived port->owner contract + ports CLI + doctor checks
description:
OBJECTIVE: Build the machine-readable port registry — the single source of truth mapping every declared port to its owning service, profile, client, and source declaration — plus CLI/doctor surfaces over it. This is Phase 0 of the port-guard stack; every later phase consumes it.

BACKGROUND: Ports today are scattered facts: runtime.yaml service healthchecks (http://localhost:8000/health), ingress_routes listeners, ~15 SKILLBOX_*_PORT env keys (.env.example), client overlay services, and docs/tailnet-ingress.md prose tables. Nothing enforces uniqueness or detects collisions; the duel rated this the non-negotiable prerequisite of all enforcement.

REASONING: you cannot block a wrong bind until "right port" is a queryable fact with provenance. The registry also upgrades agent context: generated CLAUDE.md can state exactly which port belongs to which service.

IMPLEMENTATION CONSIDERATIONS: (1) New module .env-manager/runtime_manager/port_registry.py building a registry view from the resolved runtime model: entries {port, owner_id, owner_kind (service|ingress|env_surface), client, profiles, bind_scope (loopback|tailnet|wildcard), source (file+key), protocol}. Parse ports from healthcheck targets, ingress listeners, declared `port`/env fields; tolerate unparseable health targets with a warning entry. (2) New CLI: `manage.py ports` (list, --format json/text) and `manage.py ports --resolve <service-id>`; register in command_registry.py (tier 2, surface cli+mcp, mcp_tool skillbox_ports, side_effect none, risk low) per AGENTS.md rules for new agent-facing commands. (3) Doctor checks: PORT_COLLISION (two active-scope owners, same port), PORT_WILDCARD_BIND (0.0.0.0 declared while box posture is tailnet_only), PORT_UNDECLARED_RESERVED (port inside a declared reserved range with no owner). (4) Context rendering: add a Ports table to generated agent context so in-box agents see the contract without asking. (5) Expose port attributes on service nodes in the agent ops graph.

FILES: runtime_manager/port_registry.py (new), scripts/lib/runtime_model.py (port extraction helpers), cli.py, command_registry.py, .env-manager/mcp_server.py (mirror), context_rendering.py, validation/doctor wiring, tests/test_agent_ops_command_registry.py goldens.

RISKS: health targets without ports (cfo declares `localhost:8050` w/o scheme; some checks are path_exists) — extraction must be conservative, never guess; client overlays loaded only when client active — registry is scope-aware, collisions checked within the ACTIVE scope plus a cross-client advisory mode.

ACCEPTANCE: (1) `manage.py ports --format json` lists every port declared in the active scope with owner + source; (2) fixture with duplicate port -> doctor fails PORT_COLLISION naming both declarations; (3) wildcard fixture under tailnet_only -> PORT_WILDCARD_BIND; (4) capabilities payload includes ports command; (5) generated context contains the ports table; (6) registry golden added to agent-ops goldens.

TESTING: unit tests for extraction (each source kind, malformed targets), collision/wildcard doctor fixtures, registry golden, MCP mirror smoke test, context drift golden regenerated deliberately.

OBSERVABILITY: doctor findings carry source provenance; ports command is read-only.

MAINTAINER NOTES: Keep the registry derivational — it must never become a second place to declare ports. If a port is not derivable from existing manifests, the fix is to enrich the manifest schema, not to hand-edit the registry.
close_reason: Phase 0 complete: port_registry.py builds scope-aware port->owner view with provenance (conservative extraction, never guesses ports); manage.py ports CLI + skillbox_ports MCP; PORT_COLLISION/PORT_WILDCARD_BIND/PORT_UNDECLARED_RESERVED doctor checks + cross-client advisory; context ports table + graph node attrs; 98 focused tests green

title: Dev-command intercept: PreToolUse hook + PATH shims for dev servers
description:
OBJECTIVE: Intercept dev-server launches that bypass the runtime: a PreToolUse Bash hook plus PATH shims for npm/pnpm/yarn/vite/next that block direct `dev` invocations inside managed repos and answer with the exact runtime command to use instead. Duel Phase 1, highest average score (810).

BACKGROUND: The observed failure mode is agents running `npm run dev` directly in tmux panes, spawning duplicate Vite servers on hopped ports. guard-destructive-op.sh proves the PreToolUse hook template works (matcher -> structured block). Nothing intercepts dev commands today.

REASONING: the cheapest moment to stop a rogue listener is before the process exists, with a message that teaches the contract ("use: python3 .env-manager/manage.py up --client X --service Y"). Shims catch full-path/tmux bypasses that never traverse the agent harness hook.

IMPLEMENTATION CONSIDERATIONS: (1) scripts/guard-dev-port.sh PreToolUse hook: match Bash tool calls whose command contains dev-server signatures (npm run dev, pnpm dev, yarn dev, vite, next dev, astro dev — keep the list in one table); resolve cwd -> managed repo via the port registry/runtime model; if the repo maps to a covered service, exit 2 with: owning service id, declared port, exact up command, and the escape hatch. Unmanaged repos pass through. (2) Shim directory (e.g. ${SKILLBOX_HOME_ROOT}/.local/skillbox-shims) with tiny wrappers for the same binaries: when SKILLBOX_MANAGED_RUN=1 (exported by runtime_ops service launch) they exec the real binary; otherwise same registry lookup + block message; installed by `make wrappers-install` and prepended to PATH by focus/context env. (3) Escape hatch: SKILLBOX_PORT_GUARD=off bypasses both layers, loudly logged — operators stay sovereign. (4) Register the hook in .claude/settings.json; document the codex-side equivalent limitation honestly.

FILES: scripts/guard-dev-port.sh (new), shim templates (new, under scripts/ or .env-manager/assets/), Makefile (wrappers-install), runtime_ops.py (export SKILLBOX_MANAGED_RUN for launched services), context/focus PATH wiring, .claude/settings.json, docs.

RISKS: false positives on `npm run dev` in a repo whose service is NOT covered (must pass through); shims must never break non-dev subcommands (npm install) — wrappers inspect argv and only gate the dev table; PATH injection must not leak into unrelated host shells (scope to in-box agent env and focus-generated env only).

ACCEPTANCE: (1) hook blocks `npm run dev` in a covered repo with remediation text containing the literal up command; (2) `npm install` and dev in uncovered repos pass; (3) shim blocks full-path bypass in tmux (no hook present); (4) SKILLBOX_MANAGED_RUN=1 passes; (5) SKILLBOX_PORT_GUARD=off passes and logs; (6) shellcheck clean.

TESTING: shell-harness tests (existing test_operational_scripts.py pattern) covering the matrix above; unit test that runtime_ops exports the managed-run marker; wrappers-install idempotency test.

OBSERVABILITY: every block/bypass appends a structured line (tool, cwd, matched signature, verdict) to logs/runtime/runtime.log so Phase-6 telemetry can count interceptions.

MAINTAINER NOTES: The block message IS the product — it converts a frustrated bypass into a taught contract. Keep it under 10 lines, lead with the exact command.
close_reason: Implemented dev-command guard hook, shims, runtime marker, and tests

title: Post-bind verification: enforce declared ports in service start/reuse
description:
OBJECTIVE: After the runtime starts (or adopts) a service, verify the process actually listens on its declared port; on mismatch, stop it and return a structured LOCAL_RUNTIME_PORT_MISMATCH error with observed-vs-declared and remediation. Duel Phase 2 — the sharpest single code-gap fix (scores 763-845).

BACKGROUND: runtime_ops.py start paths (_start_service / _healthy_service_start_result / _reused_existing_service_result) treat "process up + healthcheck passed" as success. Vite's auto-hop defeats this: the healthcheck URL on the declared port can even hit a DIFFERENT pre-existing listener while the new process binds port+1 — verified as a real code-path miss during the duel.

REASONING: this is the only layer that catches a wrong bind by a service the runtime itself launched, closing the loop between declaration (registry) and reality (kernel listener table).

IMPLEMENTATION CONSIDERATIONS: (1) After health-wait, resolve the listener set of the service's process tree (pid + descendants) by parsing `ss -tlnp` output or /proc/net/tcp+/proc/<pid>/fd (stdlib-only; prefer ss with /proc fallback; both behind one helper for testability). (2) Compare against the registry's declared port(s) for the service: exact match -> success enriched with verified_port; bound elsewhere -> stop the started process group, return LOCAL_RUNTIME_PORT_MISMATCH {declared, observed, owner_of_observed?, next_actions:[free the port / fix repo config / see .skillbox-port.env]}; bound nowhere after grace (non-listening task-like service) -> only enforce when the service declares a port. (3) Reuse path: when adopting an existing healthy process, run the same verification before reporting reuse. (4) Add a small retry window (e.g. 3x1s) for slow binds before judging. (5) New error code registered alongside LOCAL_RUNTIME_* codes in scripts/lib/runtime_model.py.

FILES: runtime_manager/runtime_ops.py, scripts/lib/runtime_model.py (error code), runtime_manager/port_registry.py (lookup helper), text_renderers.py (human rendering), tests/test_runtime_manager.py.

RISKS: services legitimately binding multiple ports (declare-all in registry; mismatch only when declared set ∩ observed set is empty); IPv6-only binds (parse both tcp/tcp6); containers/PID namespaces — in-box this is same-namespace, document that limit; killing on mismatch must use the same managed-stop path as `down` (no orphaned children).

ACCEPTANCE: (1) fixture service that binds declared port -> up succeeds, payload includes verified_port; (2) fixture binding port+1 -> service stopped, LOCAL_RUNTIME_PORT_MISMATCH with observed port; (3) reuse-adoption of a wrong-port process -> same error, not silent reuse; (4) non-port services unaffected; (5) error code documented in README error tables.

TESTING: unit tests with fake listener resolvers (no real sockets) for the decision matrix; one integration-style test using a real ephemeral python socket server to validate the ss/proc parser on Linux; regression: full lifecycle tests green.

OBSERVABILITY: runtime.log line on every mismatch (service, declared, observed, action=stopped); pulse/status surfaces last verification result per service.

MAINTAINER NOTES: Resist the temptation to "just warn" — the duel consensus was explicit that silent hops are the disease. Warn-only mode is acceptable solely via SKILLBOX_PORT_GUARD=off.
close_reason: Implemented post-bind declared-port verification with mismatch errors and tests

title: Pulse rogue-listener sentinel: scan, classify, grace, reap
description:
OBJECTIVE: Add a rogue-listener sentinel to the pulse daemon: every cycle, scan listening sockets, classify them against the port registry and managed-process ancestry, and reap unauthorized dev-server listeners after a grace window. Duel Phase 3 — the only layer covering ALL bypass paths (scores 745-795).

BACKGROUND: Shims and hooks can be bypassed (raw node invocation, processes started before guard install, tmux panes predating focus). The duel's problem statement showed four accumulated Vite rogues; a sentinel would have reaped all four. pulse.py already owns the reconcile loop, state snapshot (pulse.state.json), and runtime.log event stream — the sentinel is a natural new check.

REASONING: continuous observation beats point-in-time checks (Design Stance #8); the sentinel converts the registry from advice into an invariant the box maintains about itself.

IMPLEMENTATION CONSIDERATIONS: (1) pulse.py _scan_rogue_listeners(): enumerate listeners (same ss/proc helper as the post-bind bead — share it); classify each: registry-declared port owned by its managed process -> ok; system allowlist (sshd, tailscaled, docker-proxy, ports < 1024 unless dev-signature) -> ok; process whose ancestry chain includes a managed service launch -> ok; otherwise candidate-rogue. (2) Dev-server signature heuristic (process name/cmdline contains node+vite/next/webpack-dev-server etc.) decides enforcement class: signatures -> reap after grace; non-signatures -> report-only (never kill an operator's ad-hoc python -m http.server without explicit opt-in). (3) Grace window 15s (config SKILLBOX_PORT_SENTINEL_GRACE_SECONDS) so HMR restarts and legitimate quick rebinds survive. (4) Modes via SKILLBOX_PORT_SENTINEL=off|observe|enforce, default observe for two releases then enforce — record the flip as an explicit follow-up in the telemetry bead. (5) Wildcard binds (0.0.0.0) on tailnet_only posture escalate to enforce regardless of mode? No — keep observe honest, but mark them CRITICAL in events. (6) Every action -> runtime.log event + counters in pulse.state.json {rogues_seen, rogues_reaped, by_signature}.

FILES: .env-manager/pulse.py, shared listener helper (from post-bind bead), .env.example (new envs), tests/test_pulse*.py, docs (pulse section + tailnet lifecycle exposure rules).

RISKS: killing the wrong thing is the nightmare — ancestry resolution must be conservative (when in doubt, observe + report); PID reuse between scan and kill (re-verify cmdline immediately before SIGTERM); SIGTERM->wait->SIGKILL escalation with bounded wait; pulse cycle budget (scan must stay <100ms typical — cache /proc walks).

ACCEPTANCE: (1) fixture rogue with dev signature in enforce mode -> SIGTERM'd after grace, event logged with reason; (2) same in observe mode -> reported, alive; (3) managed service listener never flagged; (4) allowlisted system daemons never flagged; (5) pulse-status shows sentinel counters; (6) re-verification prevents PID-reuse kills (unit-tested with a swapped cmdline).

TESTING: unit tests with faked listener/process tables covering the full classification matrix; integration test with a real disposable socket process in observe mode; chaos overlap: sentinel + restart-backoff interplay test (a reaped managed-lookalike must not trigger restart storms).

title: Repo port contracts: generated .skillbox-port.env + strictPort adoption
description:
OBJECTIVE: Generate per-repo port contracts from the registry — a gitignored .skillbox-port.env in each covered repo plus strictPort guidance — so even a full-bypass dev launch crashes on the wrong port instead of silently hopping. Duel Phase 4 (scores 585-628), the complement that turns hop-prone tools honest.

BACKGROUND: Vite/Next auto-increment when the desired port is busy. With strictPort:true (Vite) / fixed PORT env (Next, Node servers), a busy declared port is a loud crash — exactly what we want once layers 1-3 exist to explain WHY. The duel was explicit: env-file + overlay-synced contracts, NOT in-repo source edits (skillbox must not commit to client repos).

REASONING: contracts-in-env make the registry's truth ambient: every tool that honors PORT/.env conventions inherits the declaration without skillbox patching repo source.

IMPLEMENTATION CONSIDERATIONS: (1) During focus/bridge/sync for a client, for each covered service with a declared port, write <repo>/.skillbox-port.env containing PORT=<declared>, HOST=<bind addr per posture>, SKILLBOX_SERVICE_ID=<id>; file is generated state — ensure .gitignore coverage via a doctor advisory (skillbox cannot edit client repo .gitignore; the advisory tells the operator the exact line to add). (2) Document (and template into overlay scaffolds) the one-line repo-side adoption: vite --strictPort with port from env, or `port: Number(process.env.PORT), strictPort: true` snippet; blueprints used by client-init get the snippet included. (3) Doctor advisory check PORT_CONTRACT_UNADOPTED (warn-level): covered web service whose repo lacks .skillbox-port.env consumption hints — heuristic, warn-only, suppressible per-service in the overlay. (4) Regeneration is idempotent and atomic (temp+rename).

FILES: runtime_manager (env bridge / focus path writing the files), overlay blueprint templates, doctor advisory, docs (local runtime profiles section), .env.example notes.

RISKS: repos that already manage PORT themselves (contract file must compose, not fight — document precedence and never overwrite repo-owned .env files; we only own the .skillbox-port.env name); generated files in repos that get committed accidentally (advisory + docs; name is distinctive and greppable).

ACCEPTANCE: (1) focus on a fixture client writes .skillbox-port.env per covered service with registry-matching values; (2) regeneration after a port change updates the file; (3) doctor advisory fires for an unadopted covered web service and is suppressible; (4) overlay blueprint scaffolds include the strictPort snippet; (5) files never written into non-covered repos.

TESTING: unit tests for generation (values, atomicity, idempotency, suppression); blueprint scaffold test asserting snippet presence; doctor advisory fixture tests.

OBSERVABILITY: sync/focus step output lists contract files written; doctor advisory carries the exact adoption snippet.

MAINTAINER NOTES: This layer alone is weak (someone deletes the env file) — it exists because combined with the sentinel it makes the WRONG path crash loudly and the RIGHT path effortless. Resist expanding it into in-repo source patching; that boundary was a duel decision.
close_reason: Implemented generated repo port contracts, strictPort blueprint guidance, and doctor advisories.

title: Port-guard regression suite + telemetry: encode the duel's 5 criteria
description:
OBJECTIVE: Encode the duel's five success criteria as an automated regression suite plus telemetry aggregation, producing the evidence that decides whether the deferred Phase-5 eBPF cage is ever needed and when the sentinel flips observe->enforce by default.

BACKGROUND: The duel ended with measurable criteria: (1) `npm run dev` blocked in one turn with exact remediation; (2) full bypass crashes via strictPort or is reaped within one pulse interval; (3) no silent port hops; (4) no multi-day rogue accumulation; (5) no surviving 0.0.0.0 dev listeners under tailnet_only. Without a harness, these decay into vibes.

REASONING: the stack spans four subsystems (hook, shims, runtime_ops, pulse); only an end-to-end suite proves the LAYERED property — each layer's misses are caught by the next.

IMPLEMENTATION CONSIDERATIONS: (1) tests/test_port_guard_regression.py: scenario tests wiring real fixture processes (tiny python socket servers masquerading via argv as vite-like signatures where needed) through the shared listener helper, hook script, and pulse classification — each of the five criteria gets at least one test, marked clearly CRITERION-1..5 in test names. (2) A manual proof script scripts/port-guard-proof.sh that runs the same scenarios against the LIVE box with verbose logging and writes a dated report under agent_ergonomics_audit/ or docs/research/ — the operator-facing acceptance artifact. (3) Telemetry rollup: extend pulse-status (and stewardship-report) with cumulative counters {hook_blocks, shim_blocks, post_bind_mismatches, rogues_seen, rogues_reaped, wildcard_criticals} and first/last timestamps; stewardship marks port-guard as assessed once 14 days of counters exist. (4) Document the enforce-flip rule: sentinel default flips to enforce when 14 consecutive days show zero false-positive reports — and record the flip itself as a config change with a dated note.

FILES: tests/test_port_guard_regression.py (new), scripts/port-guard-proof.sh (new), pulse.py/status/stewardship counter plumbing, docs.

RISKS: scenario tests spawning real processes must be hermetic (ephemeral ports, killed in teardown, skipped on unsupported platforms with explicit skip reasons); telemetry counters must survive pulse restarts (persist in pulse.state.json, monotonic).

ACCEPTANCE: (1) five criterion tests exist, named, and pass; (2) proof script produces a dated report with per-criterion PASS/FAIL on a live box; (3) counters persist across pulse restart; (4) stewardship-report shows the port-guard domain with evidence instead of not_assessed; (5) enforce-flip rule documented.

TESTING: this bead IS testing; additionally meta-test that criterion tests fail when a layer is deliberately disabled (mutation-style sanity for at least criterion 2 and 4).

OBSERVABILITY: the telemetry IS the observable; proof reports are dated artifacts.

MAINTAINER NOTES: Future maintainers deciding about eBPF (Phase 5): the answer lives in these counters. If layers 1-4 show leaks the sentinel cannot close, reopen the decision bead — not before.
close_reason: Implemented port-guard criterion regression suite, telemetry rollup, stewardship evidence, and proof script.

title: DECISION: eBPF bind cage (Phase 5) — gated on port-guard telemetry
description:
DECISION (deferred): Whether to build the flag-gated eBPF/cgroup bind cage (BPF_CGROUP_INET4/6_BIND behind SKILLBOX_PORT_CAGE=1) as Phase 5 of the port-guard stack.

BACKGROUND: Codex initially ranked kernel-first enforcement #1 in the 2026-06-11 duel, then conceded "Kernel-first: no. Portable-first: yes" after cross-scoring; consensus moved it to an optional Phase 5 strictly gated on telemetry showing leaks that layers 1-4 cannot close. It is the only mechanism that makes a wrong bind IMPOSSIBLE rather than detected — at the cost of kernel tooling in a deliberately thin, stdlib-first box.

DECISION RULE (agreed in the duel — do not relitigate without new evidence): build ONLY if the port-guard telemetry (see the regression+telemetry bead) shows, over at least 30 days of enforce-mode operation, recurring rogue listeners that survived a full pulse interval or wildcard binds that reached a tailnet-only box. If telemetry stays clean, close this bead as wont-fix with the counters attached.

IF BUILT: scope is a minimal cgroup-attached bind filter for the workspace container allowing only registry-declared ports + ephemeral ranges; loader is optional tooling (not a runtime.yaml-required artifact); failure mode is fail-open with a loud doctor finding (a broken cage must never brick the box); flag-gated, default off, documented as hardened mode.

ACCEPTANCE (for the decision itself): a dated decision note recorded here (and in docs/research/) citing the telemetry window reviewed, with outcome build|wont-fix; if build, spawn fresh implementation beads — do not implement under this bead.

MAINTAINER NOTES: This bead exists so the eBPF idea has exactly one home and cannot be re-pitched fresh each quarter. The duel report (DUELING_WIZARDS_REPORT_PORT_GUARD.md) holds the full scoring history.
close_reason: Operator decision 2026-06-21: drop kernel bind cage permanently; userspace enforcement sufficient. Removed moot dep on 37p9.6.

comments.text: OPERATOR DECISION 2026-06-21 (Rob): DROP the kernel eBPF/cgroup bind cage permanently. Userspace port-guard enforcement (hooks + PATH shims + post-bind verification + rogue-listener sentinel) is sufficient.

Goal: add or extend a read-only runtime evidence surface that captures the validated proof lane with stable JSON, optional markdown, and artifact-friendly command output.

Write scope: runtime manager read-only command surfaces, stewardship/report helpers, text/json renderers, docs, and focused tests. Do not mutate runtime state except optional proof artifact output chosen by the command.

Implementation shape:
- Define the scenario and baseline first: doctor summary, status/pressure, pulse status or not-running state, skills issues-only summary, MCP audit summary, git dirty summary, Beads status pointer, and next actions.
- Capture `tests/artifacts/perf/<run-id>/runtime-evidence/` before optimizing or refactoring.
- If refactoring shared pressure/status/evidence assembly, include an isomorphism proof card and golden JSON/text outputs.

Acceptance criteria:
- A read-only CLI path returns machine-readable evidence with stable top-level keys and explicit blocked/gray conditions.
- Focused tests cover success, warning, and blocked states without needing Docker up or remote provisioning.
- Existing commands retain behavior: `status`, `doctor`, `pressure-report`, `skills`, `mcp-audit`.
- Validation commands: `make doctor`, `make dev-sanity`, `python3 -m unittest tests.test_runtime_hotspot_units tests.test_pressure_report tests.test_mcp_server tests.test_cli_units`, `git diff --check`; broad unittest only after validation-trust/disk gate allows it.

Non-goals:
- Do not build a UI.
- Do not run provisioning, Docker up, or remote SSH.
- Do not optimize before a baseline/hotspot table exists.

title: Run post-SBP reality check and smart goal
description:
After the SBP visibility/MCP recalibration bead is closed, run a repo-vs-vision reality check followed by a `$smart goal` pass from this repo root.

Prompt to run:
`$reality-check-for-project + $smart goal`

The point is not a brainstorm. Compare implemented code, docs, plans, Beads, and validation commands against the project vision; then write the single most accretive smart-goal contract for the next move. If the pass discovers truly accretive follow-up work, create/update Beads with evidence and dependencies.
design:
concern: post-visibility project truth and next smart goal
writes: Beads issue notes/children and overlay-backed smart-chain artifacts if the repo has a matching invocation root

validation: repo-native validation named by the smart goal, plus Beads dependency/state check
acceptance_criteria:
- The SBP recalibration bead is closed or its unresolved blocker is explicitly accepted as not blocking this repo assessment.

- The smart goal names loop_goal, success criteria, resume condition, and validation/commit/reality-check gate.
- Any new follow-up Beads are evidence-backed, dependency-linked, and not duplicates.
- Repo-native validation commands are named or exact blockers are recorded.

title: Pressure-aware Skillbox build offload and storage guard
description:
End vision: Skillbox becomes pressure-aware for agent-heavy coding work. Local agents get explicit disk-pressure posture, large build/test commands can route to non-production remote workers through remote_compilation_helper, and storage_ballast_helper protects the operator machine and selected Skillbox boxes from disk-full incidents without touching protected agent history or production Sweet Potato infrastructure.

Default target from current evidence is the managed non-production Tailnet box `portfolio-devbox` (`portfolio-devbox.example`, <tailnet-address>), not `jeremy`, not `ssh-info`, and not `sweet-potato.example`. All destructive cleanup/install/deploy work must remain blocked until the target and policy are reverified in a child issue.
acceptance_criteria:
Epic is complete only when:
- Skillbox has a read-only pressure/build-offload report that can name disk pressure, protected paths, cleanup candidates, RCH posture, and SBH posture.
- RCH and SBH are optional managed artifacts/services/checks in the runtime graph, with safe disabled-by-default behavior.
- Agent context/focus/stewardship surfaces tell agents when to avoid local builds and how to route expensive build/test commands.
- `portfolio-devbox` is validated as the non-production Tailnet target before any remote install/deploy/probe.
- `jeremy`, `ssh-info`, and `sweet-potato.example` are explicitly excluded from write/deploy actions.
- Tests/docs are updated and repo-native validation passes or concrete blockers are recorded.
close_reason: Epic acceptance met. Skillbox now has read-only pressure-report/rch-report/sbh-report surfaces; pressure-tools optional RCH/SBH artifacts, services, checks, env defaults, compose env, and dependency inventory; pressure/offload advisory in status, compact status, generated agent context, focus/stewardship summaries, and pulse state; docs and robot discovery updated. portfolio-devbox was revalidated as the non-production Tailnet target before closeout, and jeremy/ssh-info/sweet-potato.example remain explicit exclusions. Validation: 66 focused tests OK, git diff --check OK, capabilities/robot-docs/status/render OK, br dep cycles count 0. make doctor/dev-sanity blockers recorded as existing stale skill installs only. No cleanup/delete/prod mutation/commit performed.

title: No-ragrets push readiness closeout for 38 unpushed Skillbox commits
description:
Future success: origin/main contains the 38 local commits plus any required closeout fixes, and a fresh clone can trust the pushed tree.

Outcomes:
- All current dirty/untracked artifacts are either committed intentionally or removed/reworked before push.
- The broken install verification lane is fixed or explicitly quarantined with a narrower, documented command; no temp runtime process keeps .skillbox-state busy after tests.
- Existing wave-4 no-ragrets hardening children are closed or intentionally deferred with evidence.
- Full repo validation, secret/generated-noise scan, and independent reviewer pass before push.
- Push happens only after validation/review evidence is current.

Failure avoided: pushing an open-source repo with broken internal references, leaking local/private state, a failing install test, or unreviewed agent-generated artifacts.
design:
write_scope: repo-wide closeout, but code edits must be owned by child Beads
stop_rules:
  - Do not push while tests are red, dirty artifacts are unexplained, or reviewer has unresolved blockers.
  - Do not delete or revert user/agent work without first classifying it as generated noise or moving it into a committed/closed Bead.
  - Do not include secrets, private overlays, .env/.env.box, workspace/secrets, or runtime state.
validation_order:
  1. close concrete blockers
  2. sync Beads
  3. full validation
  4. independent reviewer
  5. commit
  6. push
acceptance_criteria: Done only when: git status is clean before final push; br ready is empty or any remaining open issues are deliberately deferred and not push blockers; git diff --check, make doctor, make dev-sanity, python3 -m unittest discover -s tests, MCP audit, and secret/noise scan pass; an independent subagent review reports no push blockers; commits are created; git push succeeds and branch is no longer ahead of origin/main.
close_reason: Push readiness closeout complete. All child blockers closed; full validation passed; independent reviewer reported no push blockers; main readiness commit b8db898 pushed to origin/main. Final Beads bookkeeping will be synced, committed, and pushed as part of this closeout.

title: Fix install --verify test leak before push
description: Push blocker: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests hung in tests.test_install_script.InstallScriptTests.test_verify_runs_post_install_checks. Focused rerun failed after 159s with OSError Errno 66 Directory not empty: temp skillbox/.skillbox-state. Evidence showed install.sh --verify ran first-box -> acceptance and left a pulse runtime process with cwd inside the temp checkout, keeping cleanup busy.\n\nFix direction: make install verification/tests deterministic and self-cleaning. Prefer no-infra/no-daemon behavior for installer tests or explicit teardown of processes launched under a temp repo. Do not weaken real first-box acceptance semantics for users.
design:
writes:
  - install.sh
  - tests/test_install_script.py
  - maybe .env-manager/runtime_manager/workflows.py only if root cause is product-side process lifecycle
stop_rules:
  - If fixing requires changing real first-box acceptance behavior, split a product bug and keep installer test coverage explicit.
  - Do not hide failures by deleting the test or removing --verify coverage.
validation:
  - python3 -m unittest tests.test_install_script.InstallScriptTests.test_verify_runs_post_install_checks
  - python3 -m unittest tests.test_install_script
  - ps/lsof check for temp-root processes when diagnosing
acceptance_criteria: Focused test passes: python3 -m unittest tests.test_install_script.InstallScriptTests.test_verify_runs_post_install_checks. Full install-script module passes. No process remains with cwd under the temp repo after the test. Broad unittest can pass through this test without hanging. git diff --check clean.
close_reason: Reworked installer tests to use a minimal fake source/manage.py fixture instead of invoking real first-box/acceptance from unit tests. Validation: python3 -m py_compile tests/test_install_script.py; python3 -m unittest tests.test_install_script.InstallScriptTests.test_verify_runs_post_install_checks; python3 -m unittest tests.test_install_script; git diff --check. Process check found no install.sh/first-box/acceptance/pulse processes left by the run.

title: Independent reviewer signoff and recursive fix loop before push
description: User requested an independent reviewer subagent before push. This issue gates final commit/push after local validation.\n\nFix direction: launch one focused reviewer subagent over the final diff and validation evidence. Treat reviewer findings as push blockers unless they are clearly false positives with evidence. Recursively fix and re-review until no blockers remain, then commit and push.

  - Do not push with dirty worktree after commit.
  - If remote push rejects, fetch/rebase only after inspecting remote change risk.
acceptance_criteria: Reviewer receives current diff/status/validation evidence and reports no Critical/High push blockers. Any reviewer blocker is fixed and revalidated before commit. Final commit(s) include all intended code/docs/tests/Beads; br sync --flush-only has run; git status clean after commit; git push origin main succeeds; git status --branch no longer reports ahead commits.

title: Enforce Read-before-Edit in loop/smart skill templates
description:
Friction: The Edit tool requires a prior Read of the target file, but agents in /loop /smart cycles jump straight to editing files identified from scan output without reading them first. In session e8ee60ce (10,641 lines, 2,727 tool calls), this happened 32 times across 31 unique .tsx files — 64 wasted tool invocations (error + Read + retry). The agent identifies targets from jq output, then calls Edit without Read, gets rejected, has to Read, then retry.

Cass evidence: session e8ee60ce lines L2757-L10312 — 32 Edit-without-Read errors, each followed by Read + retry. 64 wasted tool calls in a single session.

Lube fix (smallest durable unblocker): Add a Read-before-Edit invariant to the /smart loop template or drift-detector skill. When the skill identifies a file to modify, emit a Read call before the Edit. This is a one-line change to the skill's planning prompt or template.

No-ragrets contract:
- Outcome: /loop /smart cycles never waste tool calls on Edit-without-Read errors.
- Evidence: 32 occurrences (64 wasted calls) in one session — the most frequent single friction point observed.
- Failure avoided: agent burns 2 extra tool calls per file modification in a loop that touches 100+ files.
- Acceptance: (1) smart/loop template includes Read-before-Edit guidance, (2) drift-detector skill emits Read before Edit in its action plan, (3) zero Edit-without-Read errors in next /loop /smart run.
close_reason: Added Read-before-Edit invariant to smart and loop skill templates
